Feast of #Debre #Qusquam
(Hidar 6 )

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings , we greet you with the peace of God. Today, in honor of the Feast of Debre Qusquam, we offer you this important teaching and encourage you to read and learn from it.

✍🏾The Holy Mountain of Qusquam

Mount Qusquam is a mountain in southern Egypt. Mount Qusquam is the place where Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, along with Saint Joseph and Saint Salome, rested when they returned from exile.

✍🏾Mount Qusquam is also the place where our Lord Jesus fled from those who wanted to kill Him and found refuge, and where Saint Gabriel announced to Saint Joseph in a dream that King Herod had died.

✍🏾This is according to the Holy Gospel: when Herod wanted to kill Christ, the angel of God, Saint Gabriel, appeared to the aged Joseph in a dream and said, "Take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt" (Matthew 2:13–15).

✍🏾Testimony of Saint Theophilos

✍🏾Mount Qusquam is blessed and sanctified because our Lord performed many miracles there. Regarding the sacredness of this mountain, Saint Theophilos, Archbishop of Alexandria, said in his sermon on the Assumption of Mary: "This is a mountain that is higher than all the mountains of the world. In it dwells the Holy God. The Son of God loved and honored this mountain, and He dwelled with His Holy Mother above all the nations of the world. He did not choose to dwell in the house of the angels, nor did He choose Bethany, but rather dwelt in a monastery on the mountain, as the prophet David said . loved Mount Zion and built his temple there."

✍🏾Fulfillment of the Prophecy

The persecution of Christ was fulfilled in accordance with what was foretold by the prophet Isaiah:

"Behold, the Lord will come upon a swift cloud into Egypt, and the idols of Egypt shall bow down before Him" (Isaiah 19:1).

The “swift cloud” mentioned by the prophet describes our Lord’s descent into Egypt on the back of Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary.

✍🏾During this time of persecution, the idols of Egypt were seen being shattered and falling, and the demons who had misled people through these idols were seen fleeing.

✍🏾Moreover, since our Lord is the Second Adam, He was exiled to redeem the first Adam, who had been exiled because of the deceit of Jesse (the devil), and in this way, He expelled the demons from the hearts of men.

👉🏾The Blessing of Debre Qusquam

✍🏾Our Lady blessed and sanctified Mount Qusquam, where she rested when she returned from exile with her Son. Regarding this mountain as a holy place, Saint Theophilos, Archbishop of Alexandria, said in his sermon on Mary:

👉🏾"This is a mountain higher than all the mountains of the world, in which the Holy God dwells. The Son of God loved and honored this mountain, and He dwelt with His Holy Mother above all the nations of the world. He did not choose to dwell in the house of angels, nor did He choose Bethany, but stayed in a monastery on this mountain, just as the prophet David loved Mount Zion and built his temple there."

👉🏾"When you became the dwelling place of God, O mountain, perfect joy was made between the cherubim and seraphim, and the angelic host served their Holy Creator and Lord. You, O mountain, are higher than all mountains, even Mount Sinai, for our Lord abode in you. When our Lord dwelled on Mount Sinai, there was perfect joy and great light, yet no one except Moses could approach and see Him. Even he could not behold His face. No one in flesh can see Him and live. But we have seen Him and understood His abode, and we have seen Him again in the pure Mary. From our holy Mother Mary, who was united with us in Bethlehem in flesh, He came in darkness and the shadow of death to save us because of His kindness and love for mankind. When people sinned by worshiping idols more than all the world, He descended into Egypt and revealed His great glory, shining the light of His divinity upon them." (Dirsane Mariam)

👉🏾The Mystery of Hidar 6

✍🏾On Hidar 6, as read from the Book of the Sinksar, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, in later times, gathered the apostles together at Mount Qusquam, venerated the ark and the church, offered a sacrifice, and gave them His holy body and precious blood. (Hidar Sinksar)

#Saint #George (#Hidar 7)

Dear followers of the Orthodox faith  peace be unto you. Today we present a refined teaching on the life of the Great Martyr Saint George. May it strengthen your faith.

✍🏾The Birth and Early Life of Saint George

saint George, the Great Martyr, whose name means “bright star” or “sun,” was born in Palestine in the city of Lydda. He was born on Tir 20, 277 AD.

His father, Zorothos (Anastasius), was a nobleman of Lydda. His mother, Theobsta (Ecclesia), was a devout Christian woman. Besides Saint George, she had two daughters named Martha and Asia.

When Saint George was ten years old, his father passed away. A righteous Christian king took him in and raised him with love. Under this prince, George learned military discipline and grew in both strength and wisdom.

When Saint George reached twenty years of age, the king had a beautiful fifteen-year-old daughter. During a great feast, the prince declared, “Let George marry her and inherit all my possessions.” Soon after making this promise, our Lord, whose will was different, took the soul of the king.”This saddened George deeply, and after completing the days of mourning, he traveled to Beirut.

✍🏾Saint George in Beirut

At that time, the people of Beirut worshipped a dragon and even sacrificed their own daughters to it. Seeing this terrible practice, Saint George confronted the dragon. Armed with faith and the power of the Holy Cross, he defeated the dragon and turned the hearts of the people toward the worship of the true God.

✍🏾Confession of Faith Before Seventy Kings

When Saint George later returned to Persia, Emperor Dudianus assembled seventy kings and set up seventy idols for worship. Seeing this, and being committed to the Christian faith, Saint George boldly entered the palace and confessed before them all that he was a follower of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

Dudianus, recognizing him, said, “You are one of us. I will appoint you ruler over ten regions if you worship my god Apollo.”
Saint George answered, “Your titles and rewards belong to you. I will not deny my Lord Jesus Christ.”

In rage, Dudianus ordered severe tortures. But Saint George prayed, “Do not take my life until I have put this apostate to shame.” God heard him and strengthened him. Even after dying three times from torture, the Lord raised him again, granting him great endurance.

✍🏾The Sufferings of Saint George

Among the many torments he endured:

• He was tied to a tree and beaten while his flesh was torn with iron.

• Iron shoes with long nails were forced onto his feet, and he was ordered to walk.
God sent Saint Michael to heal him

• He was pierced with seventy nails, burned on the head, struck with a hammer, and rolled with a wooden beam tied to his stomach.

• His flesh was cut with a saw, and salt was sprinkled onto the wounds.

• His body was chopped into pieces, yet our Lord Jesus Christ healed him at midnight and strengthened him again.

The Lord said to him, “You will struggle for My name for six more years. You will die three times and rise in the fourth time. I will not leave you in your sufferings.”

✍🏾 His Martyrdom and Burial

“Hidar 7 is the day on which the Holy House of Saint George is celebrated, the faithful witness of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the sun of Persia and Lydda, the star of Tarsus and Beirut, the light of the sea and the radiance of the day.”

Saint George completed his martyrdom on Miyaziya 23. The faithful prepared precious garments and perfumes, wrapped his holy body, and brought it to Lydda. But upon arrival, they found that his entire family his father Zorothos, his mother Theobsta, his sisters Martha and Asia, and his betrothed had passed away.

An uncle named Andrew received the body. The people gathered, and the Archbishop of Jerusalem, Abba Tewodros, was called. He consecrated a church in Saint George’s honor and placed the holy body there with reverence. From that day, many miracles were manifested.

✍🏾Honoring Saint George in Ethiopia

Our wise King Menelik brought soil from the tomb of Saint George in Lydda, transporting it by ship and mule. He used this holy soil as the foundation when building the church of Saint George, surrounding it with strong, blessed walls.

✍🏾Feast Days of Saint George

The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church honors Saint George on:

• Miyaziya 23 – His day of rest (martyrdom)

• Hidar 7 – The celebration of his liturgy and the feast of his Holy House.

• Tir 18 – The commemoration of his burial (Zerwote Atsmu).

#Anqetse #Bitsuan (“Blessed are those who #hunger and #thirst for #righteousness, for they shall be filled.”)
#Matthew 5:6; #Luke 6:21

(Part 19)

Dear beloved in Christ, followers of the Orthodox faith, we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Continuing our lesson on the holy Beatitude, “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled,” we learn that the true satisfaction of the soul comes only from God, who rewards those who seek Him with faith and sincerity.

✍🏾Hungering and Thirsting for Righteousness

✍🏾The fourth Beatitude is translated in some Amharic Bibles as “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.” Some understand this to refer to those who physically hunger and thirst during fasting, seeking righteousness through spiritual discipline. Because the expression “they shall be satisfied” can appear ambiguous, this translation is used to give clarity.

✍🏾Although we recognize the deep meaning behind hungering and thirsting for righteousness, we continue to use the phrase “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,” as it is also taught in the other Oriental Orthodox Churches and is well understood. True hungering and thirsting for righteousness includes the spiritual longing for righteousness and the willingness to struggle for it. A person who hungers for righteousness puts forth effort to obtain it, and this includes the discipline of fasting.

✍🏾For this reason, the teachers of the Church explain that hungering and thirsting for righteousness is closely linked with fasting.

👉🏾Saint Paul teaches in Romans 14:17:

“The kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.”

👉🏾Again in 1 Corinthians 8:8 he says:“Food does not bring us closer to God; we are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.”This reveals the spiritual value of fasting.

👉🏾He further teaches in 1 Corinthians 6:13:

👉🏾“Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food; but God will destroy them both.”
Through this he shows that fasting is a work of righteousness. Therefore, fasting and thirsting for righteousness are inseparably connected.

✍🏾Since the purpose of the Church is to guide mankind toward righteousness, the ultimate goal of the Christian life is to attain righteousness. This is achieved through continuous striving. Our Lord taught in Matthew 7:7–11:

✍🏾“Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you. Everyone who asks receives; and he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened. Or which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent? If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him?” (Matthew 7:7-11)

✍🏾 In this teaching, our Lord assures us that God grants righteousness to those who earnestly seek it:

👉🏾He gives righteousness to those who ask.

👉🏾He grants righteousness to those who seek.

👉🏾He opens the door of righteousness to those who knock.

✍🏾 Just as a loving earthly father provides good gifts to his children, so our heavenly Father abundantly gives what is good to those who desire righteousness and draw near to Him with faith and sincerity.

The first step in striving for righteousness is cleansing from sin. Just as a physically ill person loses appetite and does not feel hunger or thirst, a person living in sin has little desire for righteousness. A sick person may not enjoy food even when he eats it; likewise, a sinner does not enjoy spiritual things.

But when the sick recover, their appetite returns. In the same way, when a sinner repents and washes away his sins, he begins to hunger and thirst for righteousness again. Therefore, one must separate himself from sin in order to develop spiritual hunger.

✍🏾Just as the immediate need of a hungry and thirsty person is food and water (James 2:15–16), the immediate duty of the one who hungers for righteousness is to strive for righteousness alone. And the goal of this striving must be the attainment of righteousness.

Part 20 Continues ...

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

(Part 20)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today, based on the the above mentioned title, we present to you the following teaching and entrust all of you to read and learn from it.

✍🏾“Blessed are the merciful, for they will find mercy”

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ taught in the fifth Beatitude:
“Blessed are the merciful, for they will obtain mercy.” (Matthew 5:7)

✍🏾 The Meaning of Mercy

Mercy is a union of three virtues:

👉🏾 Compassion

👉🏾 Kindness

👉🏾 Forgiveness

👉🏾Compassion is the feeling of the heart that understands others, feels for them, makes their pain our own, and moves us to help them.

👉🏾Kindness is sharing what we have wealth, knowledge, strength, and other blessings with those who lack them, expecting nothing in return.

👉🏾Forgiveness means pardoning those who have harmed us, even when they do not deserve forgiveness, and letting go of anger or punishment.

Kindness and forgiveness flow from a compassionate heart.

Church scholars teach that mercy is of two kinds:

👉🏾 Physical mercy

👉🏾 Spiritual mercy

Physical mercy is providing what a person in need lacks.

Spiritual mercy is helping a person repent from sin and return to God.

✍🏾The Square of Mercy

The place where our Lord Jesus Christ healed the sick in body through miracles and healed the sick in soul through His teachings is known as “Awde Mihret,” meaning “the Square of Mercy.”
Even today, the platform from which the Gospel is proclaimed in the church bears this name to show that the Church is the place of mercy.

The Church, redeemed by the precious blood of Christ, is where people show mercy to one another and where God shows mercy to His people. From the days of our forefathers until now, the Church has preserved this identity as the Square of Mercy.

✍🏾 God, the Source of Mercy

May the God of Mercy be the One who grants us mercy throughout our lives. In this fifth beatitude(Anketse Bitsuan), we reflect on:

👉🏾 the mercy of God

👉🏾 the power of mercy

👉🏾 and the righteous leaders who became examples of mercy.

✍🏾God is a God of mercy. He is kind and compassionate, slow to anger and full of steadfast love. Showing mercy is His nature. For this reason, the Church praises Him saying:

“Glory to the King,Glory to the God of mercy.”To show mercy is to imitate God.

King David, the one after God’s own heart, said:

👉🏾“The Lord is merciful and forgiving, slow to anger and abundant in kindness.He will not always rebuke, nor will He keep His anger forever.He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities.As the heavens are high above the earth, so great is His mercy toward those who fear Him.As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.”

✍🏾The prophet Jeremiah also declared:

✍🏾“It is because of the Lord’s steadfast love that we are not consumed,for His mercies never fail.” (Lamentations 3:22)

👉🏾This teaches us that we live only because of His unfailing compassion.

👉🏾Saint Paul wrote to the Ephesians:

“But God, who is rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us,even when we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ;by grace you have been saved.” (Ephesians 2:4–5)

To the Hebrews, he urged:

👉🏾“Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with confidence,
that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.”

👉🏾The chief apostle, Saint Peter, wrote:

✍🏾 “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to His abundant mercy, has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you, who are kept by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.” (1 Peter 1:3–5).

He affirms that we have been born again through the richness of God’s abundant mercy.

#About #bible

Question :-what is Bible 

Answer :- My Child, You ask a question as deep as the sea. To hold the Holy Bible in your hands is to hold a universe of meaning. Many in this world see it as a mere book of history, a collection of ancient laws, or a source of moral stories. But for us, the children of the Holy Church, it is something infinitely more.

Let us sit together in the stillness of our hearts and understand what this sacred treasure truly is.

It is a Love Letter from God.

Imagine you are in a distant land, far from your father's house. You are lonely, confused, and have forgotten the way home. Then, a messenger arrives, bearing a letter. It is from your Father. In it, He tells you of His boundless love for you. He reminds you who you are, where you came from, and how to find your way back to His embrace. He warns you of the dangers on the road and promises to be with you always.

This, my child, is the Holy Bible. It is God the Father's letter to His exiled children, written not with ink, but with the very breath of the Holy Spirit through the hands of His chosen prophets and apostles. As the Apostle Paul teaches, "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness" (2 Timothy 3:16).

It is the Testimony of the Living Word.

The Holy Bible is the divinely inspired collection of writings that reveals God’s work in creation, His covenant with His people, His laws, His prophets, and ultimately His salvation given through our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

The Bible is not a book about many things; it is a book about One Person: our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ. He is the Living Word of God, and the Bible is the written Word that points to Him on every page.

In the Old Testament, He is promised, prophesied, and foreshadowed. Adam is a type of Christ who was to come. The sacrifice of Isaac points to His sacrifice. The Ark of Noah is a symbol of the salvation in His Church. The prophets spoke of His coming, His suffering, and His glory. Our Lord Himself said to those who studied the scriptures without seeing Him: "You search the scriptures, for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and these are they which testify of me" (John 5:39).

In the New Testament, He is revealed. The Gospels are the icon of His life on earth. The Epistles are the explanation of His life within us. The Revelation of St. John is the vision of His ultimate victory.

It is a Pharmacy for the Soul.

The Holy Fathers, like St. John Chrysostom, do not call the Bible a library, but a spiritual pharmacy. Are you sick with the fever of anger? There is a psalm to cool you. Are you wounded by the arrow of despair? There is a Gospel passage to be a healing balm. Are you weak from the temptations of the flesh? There is an apostolic word to give you strength.

It is food for the hungry, water for the thirsty, and a lamp for those walking in darkness. As the Prophet-King David sings, "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Psalm 118:105, LXX).

It is the Book of the Church.

This is a truth of great importance, my child. The Bible did not fall from heaven into the hands of individuals. It was born from the womb of the Holy Church. It was the Church that wrote it, the Church that compiled it, the Church that preserved it, and it is only within the Church, guided by her Holy Tradition, that it can be truly and safely understood. To try and interpret the Bible on your own, apart from the mind of the Holy Fathers who have guided us for two thousand years, is to set sail on a vast ocean without a compass or a rudder.

Our Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in its ancient wisdom, has preserved the fullness of this divine letter, including sacred books like Enoch and Jubilees, which testify to the richness of the faith handed down to us.

So, when you next pick up the Holy Bible, do not treat it as any other book. First, make the sign of the cross. Say a prayer, asking the Holy Spirit who inspired its words to illuminate your mind. Read it not to win arguments, but to meet Christ. Read it slowly, and let its words wash over you, cleanse you, and heal you.

It is God Himself speaking to you. Listen with all your heart.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

The #Afterlife of #Animals

Question :-Will animals go to heaven? My friemd was making reference to Romans 8:21-22 Any information on animal afterlife?

Answer :-My dear child, your question about animals in the afterlife, and your friend's reference to the powerful words of St. Paul in Romans 8:21-22, touches a chord in many hearts, for indeed, we witness the suffering of all creation and naturally yearn for its redemption. It is a compassionate and insightful question.

Let us turn our hearts and minds to the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, as revealed in Scripture and understood by the Holy Fathers.

You mentioned:
👉🏾Romans 8:21: "Because the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God."

👉🏾Romans 8:22: "For we know that the whole creation groans and labors with birth pangs together until now."

These verses are profoundly significant. St. Paul is speaking here of the cosmic redemption that awaits all creation, not just humanity. When Adam and Eve fell into sin, their sin had repercussions not only for humanity but for the entire created order, subjecting it to decay, suffering, and death what St. Paul calls "the bondage of corruption." The "groaning" of creation is its suffering under the curse of sin, awaiting its liberation.

Now, concerning animals specifically and their place in this redemption:

1.  The Restoration of Creation, Not Individual Animal Souls in the Human Sense:

The Orthodox understanding, drawing from the Fathers, emphasizes that while God loves and cares for all His creation, the "heaven" or eternal life promised to humanity is fundamentally different from what might be understood for animals.

✍🏾Human beings are created in the image and likeness of God, possessing an immortal, rational, spiritual soul capable of communion with God, of moral choice, repentance, and personal salvation unto deification (theosis). Our eternal destiny is a personal, conscious relationship with the Creator in His Kingdom.

✍🏾Animals possess a "soul" (psyche or nephesh* in Hebrew, meaning "life principle"), which gives them life, sensation, and instinct. However, this is generally understood not to be an immortal, rational, spiritual soul in the same way as human souls. Animals do not have moral responsibility, nor do they seek personal communion with God in the way humans do. Therefore, their "salvation" or "afterlife" is not understood in terms of individual, conscious, eternal existence in the same manner as for humans.

2.  The New Heavens and New Earth:

When St. Paul speaks of creation being "delivered from the bondage of corruption," he points to the New Creation—the "new heavens and a new earth" spoken of in Isaiah (65:17) and Revelation (21:1). This will be a transfigured, glorified creation, where the effects of the Fall are utterly removed. There will be no more suffering, decay, or death.

In this renewed creation, it is a pious and beautiful hope that animals, in some transfigured form, will indeed be present. The Prophet Isaiah gives us wonderful imagery of this harmonious new creation: "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them" (Isaiah 11:6, Septuagint). This suggests a world where the natural order, currently scarred by predation and suffering, is restored to its original peaceful state of harmony as God intended.

3.God's Love and Providence for All:

Our Lord Himself taught that not a single sparrow falls to the ground without our Father's knowledge (Matthew 10:29). This speaks to God's immense providence and love for all His creatures. While we may not fully comprehend the ultimate destiny of individual animals, we trust in God's perfect wisdom and goodness, knowing that His plan for the restoration of creation is comprehensive and glorious.

So, to summarize, my dear child: the Holy Scriptures and the wisdom of the Fathers point to a future where all creation, including the animal kingdom, will be freed from the corruption and suffering caused by sin, participating in the glorious liberty of the children of God in the new heavens and new earth. While this is not understood as individual animals having an immortal soul and conscious eternal life like humans, it is a profound affirmation of God's love and ultimate redemption for everything He has made.

May this bring comfort to your heart and to your friend's, knowing that God's mercy extends to all His works.

#Feast #of #Angels (Hidar 13)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teaching we greet you with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you this important teaching, and we entrust you to read and learn from it:

✍🏾 “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to serve those who will inherit salvation?” Heb. 1:14

✍🏾 On this day, our Church Fathers instruct us to commemorate the Feast of the Holy Angels, celebrated on Hidar 13.

✍🏾 The Church celebrates this feast according to the order established by our Fathers, who were guided by the Holy Spirit.


✍🏾The Ministry of the Holy Angels

The first and highest ministry of the holy angels is to praise the God who created them. In their unceasing worship they glorify, honor, and exalt Him, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits, your creation fills the earth.” Enoch 9:39; Isaiah 6:2-4.

As it is written: “You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things, and by Your will they existed and were created.” Revelation 4:11.

The angels praise the God of gods, the Lord of lords, and the King of kings.

👉🏾Saint John the Evangelist also describes their worship:
“I looked and heard the voice of many angels around the throne… and their number was myriads of myriads. They said with a loud voice, ‘Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.’ And every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth, and in the sea said, ‘Blessing and honor and glory and might be to the One seated on the throne and to the Lamb forever and ever.’” Revelation 5:11-14.

In addition to this divine ministry of praise and thanksgiving, the holy angels also serve as manifestations of the power, goodness, and mercy of their Creator toward His creation. Their ministry is especially revealed in their care for Adam and all his children throughout history.

✍🏾The Meaning of Their Names

The names used for angels in Scripture and in the tradition of the Church all point to their identity as messengers and servants of God. Each term highlights a different aspect of their ministry.

• (መላክ)Melak
Means “to send.” The root shows their role as those who are sent by God.

• (ላኪ )Laki
Means “the one who is sent” or “the sender.”
Example: “When the Jews sent to ask him…” John 1:19.

• (ተልእከ) (Tel-e-k)
Means “sent” or “one who serves.”
Example: “She arose and served them.” Matthew 8:15.
It shows the angelic role of carrying out God’s works.

• Servant
A general meaning, expressing their obedience and service to the will of the Creator.

• (ልኡክ) Li-uk
Means “sent, messenger, servant.”
Example: “The messenger of our Lord…” 1 Peter 1:1.
This emphasizes both being sent and being a servant.

• “Emissary”
Used in the Acts of the Apostles to describe one who is dispatched for a divine purpose.

• (ላእከ) La-e-ke
Means “messenger” or “servant.”
Example: “They are messengers…” Romans 13:4.

• Message
This refers to a written message or letter, such as “The Epistle of the Apostle John.” 1 John 1:1.
The word connects angels with the concept of delivering God’s message.

• Angel
According to Amharic grammar, “angel” means a messenger of God, a heavenly and divine being created to serve His will.

✍🏾Their Nature

The nature of the holy angels is subtle and spiritual. They are spirits, not physical beings.
They cannot be touched or seen with bodily eyes, they have no flesh and bones, they do not marry, and they are not given in marriage, meaning they have no natural power to reproduce.(Luke 24:39, Matthew 22:30)

Teachings of the Church Scholars About the Nature of Angels

The scholars of the Church have handed down two explanations regarding the nature of the angels:

1.Created from wind and fire

This view teaches that angels were created from a spiritual and fiery nature.
Its basis is Psalm 103:4:
“He makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.”

According to this understanding, angels are described as spiritual beings with a fiery, luminous nature, fitting their role as God’s servants and messengers.

2. “Unsearchable nature” (A nature known only to God)

Another teaching of the Church Fathers states that the nature of angels is mysterious and cannot be fully described, for it is known only to God.

Saint Epiphanius of Cyprus, in his book Aximaros, argues that if angels were simply made of wind and fire, then death would have power over them, since these elements belong to the created world.He notes that even Adam, while in the flesh, triumphed over death by God’s grace.

Therefore, Epiphanius teaches that the angels’ nature is not of earthly or elemental substance, but from a hidden nature known only to God.
As he writes:“No one knows what the nature of angels is, except God alone.”

He also teaches that God created the angels on Sunday and established them in three heavenly ranks:Ior, Rama, and Erer (as recorded in Aximaros).

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets

Fasting of the Prophets: This is one of the seven great fasts of the Church. It is observed every year from Hidar 15 until the eve of the Nativity.

✍🏾 The Fast of the Prophets lasts for 44 days before the Nativity. During this fast, the faithful remember the fulfillment of the prophecies spoken by the prophets and the completion of the 5500 years of human suffering.

✍🏾When God the Father willed to save the world, the prophets guided by the Holy Spirit prophesied in every generation about:

👉🏾 His taking on human flesh

👉🏾 His flight into Egypt

👉🏾 His baptism in the Jordan River

👉🏾 His enlightening the darkened world through His teaching

👉🏾 His suffering for the salvation of mankind

👉🏾 His crucifixion and death

👉🏾 His resurrection, ascension, and second coming

✍🏾 The prophets longed to see these prophecies fulfilled. They prayed and fasted, saying, “Stretch out Your strength and stretch out Your hand.” They counted days, weeks, months, and years, waiting for the moment when God would become man for the salvation of the world.

✍🏾Names and Significance of the Fast

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets is called the “Fast of the Prophets (tsome Nebiyat)” because it commemorates the fulfillment of the prophecies and prayers of the holy prophets who awaited the birth of our Lord.

👉🏾 It is also called the “Fast of Adam(tsome adam)” because it marks the fulfillment of the promise of salvation given to Adam.

👉🏾It is called the “Fast of the Sermon” (tsome sibket )because it is a time when the gospel about the birth of Christ is widely preached.

👉🏾The fast ends on the day of the Nativity, which is why it is also known as the “Fast of the Nativity.”(tsome lidet)

👉🏾 It is called the “Fast of the Apostles”(tsome hawaryat) because the holy apostles said, “We fast on the day of the Resurrection, and what do we do on the day of the Nativity?” They observed the fast that the prophets observed before the birth of Christ.

👉🏾 It is also called “Philip’s Fast”(tsome filipos). The Apostle Saint Philip traveled throughout Africa, teaching the Gospel in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, performing miracles, and converting many to the faith. He died as a martyr among those who rejected his teachings. When his disciples were about to bury his body, they observed a week of fasting and prayer, asking God to return the body of the apostle to them. God granted their request, and his body was returned on the third day and buried in glory.

👉🏾 After finding the body of the apostle, his disciples continued the fast until the birth of our Lord. That is why the prophets also call it “Philip’s Fast.”

✍🏾Additionally, after the angel Gabriel announced to the Holy Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of God through the Holy Spirit, our Lady observed a fast before giving birth, saying, “What shall I do, since I have conceived a God whom heaven and earth cannot contain?” This fast is therefore also known as the “Fast of Mary.”(tsome Mariam)

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets and the Period of Teaching

During this fast:

The prophets fasted and prayed.

The apostles fasted and received blessings.

The Church Fathers established the tradition that we, the faithful, should also observe this fast so that we may receive blessings like them.

✍🏾 The Season of Teaching(Astemhro)

According to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, the period from Hidar 6 to Tahisas 7or 13) is called the period of teaching (Astemhro).

Astemhro :(when it writes with the  letter “ሀ”,in Amharic alphabet ) means the time of teaching the period when the Gospel and the goodness of God are preached widely.

The root of the word is:

Mehare – taught, gave instruction, led, showed, advised.

Temhire – learned, taught.
This signifies a time when God’s goodness, compassion, patience, and saving work are widely proclaimed in the Church.

Astemhro (when it writes with “ሐ”in Amharic alphabet) also means a time of mercy and forgiveness.

The root:

Mehare – forgave, forgave a debt.

Amhare –  to please, to forgive, to show pity, to grieve.
This is a Ge’ez verb expressing acts of mercy, compassion, and intercession, showing how one responds to the needs and sufferings of others.


✍🏾 Spiritual Meaning

The period of teaching is a time when God instructs us about His goodness and mercy. He teaches that:

He forgives all our sins.

We, the faithful, should also forgive one another.

The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church observes seven officially decreed fasts. These are:

2. The Fast of the Apostles ( Tsome Hawaryat )

3. The Fast of the Assumption (St. Mary’s Fast) Tsome Felseta

4. The Fast of the Prophets (Tsome Nebiyat)

5. The Fast of Gehad or gad )

6. The Fast of Nineveh( Tsome Nenewe)

7. Tsome Dihnet :-The Weekly Fast (Wednesdays and Fridays)

These fasts have been practiced from ancient times, and each carries a spiritual purpose for the growth and salvation of the believer.

✍🏾Teachings on Fasting from the Holy Books

The Holy Scriptures, along with ancient Church books such as Haymanote Abew and Fetha Negest, give instructions on how the faithful should fast.

a. Haymanote Abew (Three Centuries), Chapter 20:18–29

Do not break the fast commanded by the Lord, especially Wednesday and Friday, unless due to sickness.

Even on major feast days such as Pentecost, Epiphany, or baptisms, Wednesday and Friday fasting is kept, except for the ill.

Those who observe Abiy Tsom must keep the fast with great care, especially during the seven days before Easter (Semune Hammamat).

If a brother visits you to eat during your voluntary fast (such as Monday, Tuesday, or Thursday), eat with him in love and good conscience, but do not neglect the mandatory fasts of Wednesday, Friday, and the Forty Days.

Fasting on Saturday until sunset is not encouraged. There are times when fasting on Saturday is appropriate, but never until the sixth or seventh hour (sunset).

On Sunday morning, go to church early, avoiding distraction, and stand with reverence throughout the Divine Liturgy, reflecting on the suffering, death, and resurrection of Christ.

The fasts of Wednesday and Friday should be kept at least until the ninth hour of the day. Fasting beyond this benefits the soul.
Do not leave church before the Liturgy concludes unless due to illness or urgent necessity.

If you are able to fast two consecutive days, do so humbly, without pride, for pride is the weapon of Satan by which he fell from glory and leads many into destruction.

Let no one compel you to fast, to prostrate on holy Sunday, for prostrating on Sunday is not accepted by the Church.Likewise, do not prostrate on the Eve of Sunday (Saturday) or on the Holy Days of Easter (Pentecost).Do not prostrate after receiving the Holy Body and Blood, whenever the Divine Liturgy is celebrated.
These practices are not derived from the apostolic tradition of the Church.

Do not fast on Sunday and Saturday as you do on other fasting days, except for one specific Saturday:

the Saturday before Easter, the day our Lord Jesus Christ was buried.

This day alone is observed with fasting because it is the day Christ rested in the tomb for our salvation.

Do not be deceived by the error of the Marqosites, who teach fasting on Sundays and Saturdays.Do not neglect the time of the Divine Liturgy.Prepare your body and soul to be worthy of receiving the precious Body and Blood of Christ.Receiving Holy Communion unworthily brings severe judgment upon a person.

When brothers visit you, do not neglect to wash their feet.The Holy Trinity will judge those who ignore this command, for the Lord Himself instructed even the bishops to wash the feet of the disciples.

This act is a sign of humility, love, and obedience to Christ’s command.

a. Learning from the Fathers

The book “Ask Your Father and He Will Tell You” teaches that we must learn how to fast from the holy fathers and follow their footsteps.

b. Teaching of Saint Epiphanius

Saint Epiphanius says:
“A person whose mother is not the Church cannot have God as Father.”
Without the Church, it is impossible to know God, and without God, it is impossible to know the Church.

Therefore, it is the duty of every Christian to:

attend church regularly

learn the Word of God

pray faithfully

receive the Holy Body and Blood of Christ . as the Fathers say, "the Church is for Christians".

This devotion should increase even more during fasts.

✍🏾The Spiritual Meaning of Fasting

During fasting:

The soul becomes master over the body.

The soul governs, instructs, and disciplines the flesh.

A person who does good becomes holy in both soul and body and inherits the Kingdom of Heaven.

One who does evil loses both body and soul to destruction.

When Scripture calls someone a sinner, it means the will of the flesh has conquered him.
When it calls someone righteous, it means he has conquered the desires of the flesh and brought his soul into obedience to God.

The life of a Christian is therefore a constant struggle between the will of the soul and the will of the flesh.

humility

prayer

repentance

(Ezekiel 8:21; Nehemiah 1:4; Daniel 9:3)

Therefore, we must enter fasting with a humble heart, seeking the mercy of God and purifying our lives through sincere repentance.

Our Lord teaches that mercy toward those in need reveals the true servant of God. In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30–37), He said:

✍🏾A man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers who stripped him, beat him, and left him half dead. A priest happened to come down that way, saw him, and passed by on the other side. Likewise, a Levite came, saw him, and passed by. He placed him on his own donkey, brought him to an inn, and cared for him. The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying, “Take care of him; and whatever more you spend, when I return, I will repay you.”

After telling the parable, the Lord said:

In this, Christ teaches that what made the Samaritan more favored than the priest and the Levite was his kindness and compassion. Mercy, not position or title, makes one pleasing to God.

Saint Paul gives the same instruction when he says:
“Remember the prisoners as if you were bound with them, and those who suffer, as if you yourselves were in the body.” (Hebrews 13:3)
We are called to stand with the suffering as though their pain were our own.

7. A Heart Filled With Mercy Shows Compassion Even to Sinners

A merciful heart does not measure a person by their failures. Instead, it sees the image of God in every soul and desires their restoration.

When the scribes and Pharisees brought to Christ the woman caught in adultery, they demanded judgment. Christ instead revealed the truth of all humanity: “Let the one who is without sin be the first to cast a stone.” When they left one by one, acknowledging their own sin, Christ told the woman, “Neither do I condemn you; go, and sin no more.” (John 8:11)

He teaches us not to stand as judges like the Pharisees, but to offer mercy as He did.

✍🏾As the Evangelist Luke writes, a Pharisee named Simon invited our Lord to eat with him. The Lord entered Simon’s house and reclined at the table. A woman from the city, known to be a sinner, heard that He was in the house. She brought an alabaster jar of perfume and stood behind Him at His feet. Overcome with sorrow, she wept, and her tears fell upon His feet. She washed His feet with her tears, wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed His feet continually, and anointed them with the perfume.

When Simon saw this, he said within himself, “If this man were truly a prophet, He would know who and what kind of woman is touching Him, for she is a sinner.” Perceiving his thoughts, our Lord spoke and said, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” Simon replied, “Speak, Master.”

Our Lord said, “A certain creditor had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they had nothing to repay, he forgave them both. Which of them, then, will love him more?” Simon answered, “I suppose the one who was forgiven more.” The Lord said to him, “You have judged rightly.”

Turning toward the woman, He said to Simon:
“Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave Me no water for My feet, but she washed My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave Me no greeting, but she has not ceased to kiss My feet from the moment I entered. You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume. Therefore I tell you: her many sins are forgiven, for she has loved much. But the one who is forgiven little loves little.”

Then He said to the woman, “Your sins are forgiven. Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

In this holy event, the Lord teaches us to show mercy rather than judgment, to welcome the repentant, and to imitate His compassion toward every sinner who returns with a humble heart.

Faithful Examples

✍🏾Saint Joseph the Righteous

Joseph held great authority in the land of Egypt, yet he showed extraordinary mercy to his brothers who betrayed him, threw him into a pit, and sold him into slavery. He forgave them without recalling the years of suffering he endured because of their actions. Instead of seeking repayment or revenge, he provided them with grain during the famine so they would not die of hunger. He welcomed them and their families to live safely in Egypt and pardoned all the wrong they had done to him.

Moses also stands as a model of mercy. He pleaded earnestly before God on behalf of the children of Israel, who repeatedly rebelled against Him. He bowed before the Lord and said:

“O Lord, this people has committed a great sin and made for themselves gods of gold. Now forgive their sin; but if not, blot me out of the book You have written.”
(Exodus 32:32)

In both examples, Moses shows a shepherd’s heart, choosing mercy even when the people had deeply wounded both God and himself.

✍🏾 The reed (Engcha) is a type of grass that grows near water. In the Old Testament, priests sometimes referred to it in their rituals, saying, “The Lord is tried, the devil is bound.” When a reed grows, it bends and lowers itself naturally.

Holy #Welete #Petros (#Hidar 17)

Dear brethren in Christ, peace be to you.Today we remember the blessed mother Saint Welete Petros, a pillar of the Orthodox faith and a defender of the Tewahedo Church during the trials of Emperor Susenyos.

✍🏾Her Birth and Family

Saint Welete Petros was born in Daro in eastern Ethiopia.
Her father was Bahir Aseged, and her mother was Christos A-E-beya.She had two brothers, Yohannes and Zedengel, who served as high officials during the reign of King Susenyos.

After the death of her father, her mother remarried a military commander and had three more children. The place where Welete Petros later lived with her husband, Bitwoded Si-Ele Kristos, still contains her historical memorial stone.

✍🏾The Crisis of Faith Under Emperor Susenyos

While she lived peacefully with her husband, Emperor Susenyos abandoned the Tewahedo faith and accepted the teachings of Roman Catholics. He commanded all Ethiopians to follow the new religion, creating deep conflict between faithful Orthodox Christians and the king’s supporters.

When her husband brought the robe of Abune Simeon as an offering to the king, showing loyalty to the Catholic influence, Welete Petros was deeply grieved. Seeing the faith of her fathers dishonored, she refused to remain in the same house with someone who had accepted heresy. She sought a way to flee and secretly contacted monks from Tana for help.

✍🏾 Her Escape and Early Monastic Life

Abba Fetele Selassie, the abbot of Tana Kirkos Monastery, sent two nuns to bring her safely to the monastery. By this time, all her children had passed away. When her husband discovered her flight, he sent soldiers to retrieve her. Yet by God’s protection, she and the two nuns hid deep within a forest until the soldiers left. The place where they concealed themselves is still known as “Saga Welete Petros,” and a church was later built there in her memory.

After escaping danger, she entered Debre Enq Monastery. There she studied the monastic rule, received the monastic tonsure, and dedicated herself fully to God. With her vows came the beginning of great persecution. As a nun, Saint Welete Petros traveled across the regions, strengthening the faithful and urging them to stand firm in the Tewahedo faith. She taught them not to speak the name of the king who had corrupted the Church during the Divine Liturgy. Through her courage and spiritual guidance, many believers remained steadfast and even embraced martyrdom rather than abandon the faith of their fathers.

✍🏾The Trials and Perseverance of Saint Welete Petros

When Emperor Susenyos heard how boldly Saint Welete Petros was strengthening the faithful, he sent soldiers throughout the regions to capture her and bring her to judgment. At last she was seized and taken before the emperor. The princes, nobles, and scholars who had abandoned the Tewahedo faith for worldly gain gathered to examine her.

Her accusers charged her with grave offenses: “You have denied the king, denied God, refused His command, insulted the religion, and hardened the hearts of the people so they would not accept the king’s new faith.” Saint Welete Petros, following the example of her Lord Jesus Christ, remained silent before their accusations. Seeing her unshaken, the emperor placed her under house arrest, ordering her to live among her relatives so she would remain under close watch.

Yet during this time, the Church was being trampled and the Orthodox faith was openly despised. The love she had for her faith and her Church would not allow her to sit quietly in exile. She escaped from the place where she was confined and traveled to Zege Monastery. There, with her two faithful companions, Welete Paulos and Ehte kristos , she encouraged the monks and the local faithful to stand firm in the Tewahedo faith.

After staying there for some time, criticism and accusations from those opposed to her mission increased. So she left Zege and journeyed to Waldiba Monastery, continuing her mission of strengthening believers wherever she went.

Continues 👇🏾‌‌

✍🏾The Ministry of Saint Welete Petros in Waldeba and Tselemt

After Saint Welete Petros entered the holy monastery of Waldeba and completed her week of spiritual preparation, she began teaching the fathers and mothers of the monastery, urging them to remain steadfast in the Tewahedo faith. Her words strengthened hearts, restored courage, and rekindled devotion among the monastics.

✍🏾When Emperor Susenyos learned how boldly she continued to resist the foreign teachings and how she strengthened the monks and the faithful to stand firm in Orthodoxy, he grew deeply troubled. Her influence was turning many back from their apostasy, and this angered him. He repeatedly sent soldiers to seize her, but while she remained in Waldeba they could not capture her. Seeing their persistence, she departed from Waldeba and journeyed to Tselemt.

✍🏾In Tselemt her teachings spread quickly, like fire racing through dry grass. The believers welcomed her with love and accepted her guidance. Many prepared themselves for martyrdom rather than abandon the faith of their fathers. Hearing this, Emperor Susenyos declared, “If I leave her alone, she will never leave me,” and commanded Balambaras Filatawos, the governor of Tselemt, to arrest her and bring her before him.

Ruth showed deep mercy toward Naomi, who had lost her husband and her two sons. Though Ruth herself had nothing, she chose to care for Naomi with unwavering devotion. She left her homeland, Moab, and journeyed with her to Bethlehem.

When Naomi urged her to return to her own people, Orpah turned back, but Ruth remained faithful to the end. Her kindness and sacrifice made her worthy of the blessing spoken to her:
“May the Lord reward you according to your work, and may your reward be full from the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.” (Ruth 2:12)

✍🏾The Widow of Zarephath

During the great famine in the days of Elijah, the widow of Zarephath had only a handful of flour and a little oil left. She told the prophet,“I am gathering sticks to prepare a meal for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die.” (1 Kings 17:12)

Even in such desperate poverty, she shared what little she had with Elijah. Because of her mercy and obedience, God blessed her household throughout the famine.

Our Lord Himself confirmed her blessedness, saying that Elijah was sent not to any widow in Israel, but to the widow of Zarephath (Luke 4:26).

✍🏾The Poor Widow

While our Lord was teaching, a poor widow came and placed two small copper coins into the treasury. Christ called His disciples and said:

“Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others. For they gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all she had to live on.”(Mark 12:42–44; Luke 21:1–4)

Her offering became a symbol of pure, heartfelt sacrifice. It is remembered in the intercessory prayer found over 260 times in the Book of Acts:

“Lord, accept the thanksgiving I offer in my time of need, remembering the thousands of angels who serve You at all times, just as You accepted the small offering of the poor woman more than those who gave from their abundance.”

Tabitha, also called Dorcas, lived in Joppa and was known for her abundant good works and almsgiving. Scripture says:

“Now in Joppa there was a certain Tabitha, full of good works and almsgiving. In those days she fell sick and died. And they laid her in an upper chamber. And when he was come, they brought him up into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood before him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them. And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up; and when he had called the saints and widows, he presented her alive.” (Acts 9:36–43)

Anba Abram is one of the saints of the twentieth century, remembered especially for his deep compassion and his countless works of mercy. Among the many stories of his kindness, the following two examples are often told:

Kindness done without love carries no spiritual value.

Therefore, let us store our treasures with God in heaven, so that our hearts may remain with Him.

Even if we have nothing and simply say with a sincere heart, “May God give us so we may give,” He sees the intention and grants according to His mercy. Proverbs 3:3

Acts 3:19-20

✍🏾 When we fast, we must also abstain from gossip, slander, adultery, false witness, and every sin that defiles the soul.

✍🏾 The foundation of fasting is obedience to God. While certain times forbid specific foods for religious reasons, fasting is not limited to food alone. The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church teaches two kinds of fasting:

👉🏾 Fasting from certain foods (such as abstaining from meat)

👉🏾 Fasting from all sin, which we must practice at all times

✍🏾 The reason we avoid certain foods is not because they are evil, but because of obedience to the spiritual order. When we willingly restrain the body, we turn our thoughts toward the heavenly life where there is no eating and drinking, and we give thanks to God.

👉🏾 In the days of the prophet Joel, when the rain ceased and the trees withered, the people received blessing during fasting and prayer (Joel 1:12-14).

✍🏾 Blessings in harvest

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾 The order of the Holy Church is guided by moderation and spiritual wisdom.

✍🏾 Many people fast until 3, 6, 7, 9, or 11 o’clock according to their custom, but the canons of the Church actually prescribe specific fasting hours.

✍🏾 In the Fetha Negest it is written:

“They shall fast until the twelfth hour, and they shall fast until the ninth hour, except on feast days such as the Nativity and Baptism which fall on Wednesdays and Fridays.”(Ft. Ngs. Art. 15:565–566)

✍🏾 After listing the fasts, the same article, in number 572, adds:

👉🏾 “They shall fast until the ninth hour in the afternoon… but whoever fasts beyond this will receive a greater reward. However, they shall not fast on Sundays and Saturdays, except by abstaining from forbidden foods.”

✍🏾 The Great Fast (Hudade) has a different order from the regular Wednesday and Friday fasts.

👉🏾 “They shall fast until sunset on the first weeks of the Great Fast. During the remaining weeks, they shall fast until the eleventh hour, but in the month of Semone Hmamat they shall fast until the rising of the star.”
(Ft. Ngs. Art. 15:595)

✍🏾 The first week of the Great Fast, known as Zewerede, is observed until the Twelfth hour.

✍🏾 In Fetha Negest number 578, it is also taught about Semone hmamat:

“They shall fast both Friday and Saturday of Semone Hmamat together, and whoever is able should not eat anything until the rooster crows at night. But whoever is unable to fast both days should at least fast on Saturday.”

✍🏾Summary of Fasting Hours in the Church

👉🏾 The Six Regular Fasts: Until the ninth hour.
(Wednesday, Friday, Gena Fast, Nineveh Fast, Apostles’ Fast, Filseta Fast)

👉🏾 Weeks of the Great Fast (except Zewerede and Hmamat): Until the eleventh hour

👉🏾 First Week of the Great Fast (Zewerede): Until the twelfth hour

👉🏾 Semone Hmamat: Until the rising of the star.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

Blessed Are the Pure in Heart

👉🏾Our Lord taught in the sixth Beatitude, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God” (Matthew 5:8). In the spiritual life, the heart holds a central place. Scripture uses the word heart to describe the whole inner life. It includes the mind, desire, emotion, and will.

✍🏾When the wise Solomon said, “My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways” (Proverbs 23:26), he was calling us to walk in the will of God. He also taught, “Keep your heart with all diligence, for from it flow the issues of life” (Proverbs 4:23). This means we must guard our inner spiritual life with care.

✍🏾Our Lord explained, “Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. A good person out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth good, and an evil person out of the evil treasure brings forth evil” (Luke 6:45). A person speaks and acts from what fills the heart. Words reveal the life within.

✍🏾He also warned, “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me” (Matthew 15:8). In other words, there are those who speak religious words, yet their actual life and actions do not reflect closeness to God.


👉🏾Saint James teaches:

“Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners; and purify your hearts, you double-minded.” (James 4:8)

✍🏾This instructs us to cleanse our inner life, the heart, so that God may draw near to us. Purity begins within. When the heart is purified, the whole life becomes aligned with God.

✍🏾A pure heart is a life free from the stains of sin, surrendered to God in love, lived with sincerity and faithfulness. It is a heart that reflects the presence of God.

The perfect example of such purity among all humanity is the Holy Virgin Mary, our Redeemer’s Mother. She is pure in spirit, pure in speech, and pure in deed.

For this reason the Church rightfully calls her:

“The purest of the pure.”

Her body was pure, her soul was pure, and her heart was pure. Because of this purity, she became the dwelling place of the Most High. The divine nature, which no creature can behold, took flesh from her and became man for our salvation.

Our holy fathers praised her, saying:

“She was pure and holy like the Ark on Sinai. She dwelt in the Temple as the Ark once dwelt in the sanctuary. Her food was heavenly, and her drink was the drink of peace.”

👉🏾Saint Dioscorus also proclaimed her purity in the Divine Liturgy, saying:

“By the will of the Father, He came down and was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, the pure one. He was born of her, He dwelt among us, He was held in the arms of His Mother, and He was nourished as a child.”

✍🏾The Main Manifestations of Purity of Heart

1. Purifying the Heart Through Repentance

Saint Paul teaches:

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)

This means no one begins with a pure heart. Purity is restored through repentance. This is why Saint David prayed:

“Create in me a clean heart, O Lord, and renew a right spirit within me.” (Psalm 51:10)

Through true repentance, God grants a renewed, purified heart.

The prophet Ezekiel also calls the people to repentance:

“Cast away from you all your transgressions by which you have sinned, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God. Therefore turn and live.” (Ezekiel 18:31–32)

This teaches that those who repent begin to form a new heart within themselves.

Again the prophet declares God’s promise:

“I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean. I will cleanse you from all your filthiness and from all your idols. I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will keep My ordinances and do them.” (Ezekiel 36:25–27)

Those who repent sincerely are washed, renewed, and given a clean heart by God’s mercy.
Blessed indeed are those whose hearts are purified through repentance, for they shall see God.

The Feast of the #Ark of #Zion (#Hidar 21)

(Part 1)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings , we greet you all with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you this important spiritual lesson. May it be read with understanding and kept with faith.

✍🏾The Meaning of Zion

The Ark of Zion is symbolically represented by our Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary. Every year on hidar 21, the Church celebrates the feast of our mother.

✍🏾 “Zion” means tower and refuge. Concerning this, the psalmist David said, “Man calls Zion our mother, and man was born in her.” (Ps. 86:5). This reveals the mystery prepared for the salvation of Adam and his children, who had been held under the condemnation of sin for five thousand five hundred years. In order to free humanity from the prison of Sheol, God the Son chose to take flesh from the Holy Virgin Mary, who was descended from the lineage of David.

✍🏾 He dwelt in her holy womb, and after nine months and five days, He was born for the salvation of the world. Therefore, we, the faithful of the Orthodox Church, honor, glorify, and give thanks to the Holy Virgin Mary. She is the dwelling place of God, the tower of refuge, and the foundation of our salvation.

✍🏾The Ark of Zion as a Type of the Virgin Mary

👉🏾The Ark of Zion is symbolized by the Virgin Mary. We celebrate her annual feast on Hidar 21st. Among the many reasons for this celebration, the most important is that the Ark of Zion shattered the idol Dagon and performed miracles during its captivity among the Philistines.

👉🏾The great prophet Moses carved two tablets of stone, built a wooden ark, and ascended the mountain as God commanded him.

👉🏾“And I made an ark of acacia wood, and hewed two tables of stone like the first, and went up into the mount, and the two tables were in my hand: and he wrote upon the tables the ten commandments, which the LORD spake unto you in the mount out of the midst of the fire, as they were written at the first: and the LORD gave them unto me.” (Deuteronomy 10:1-4)
They carried the ark of the covenant with them and entered the land of their possession.

👉🏾While Zion is a symbol of our Lady, the Virgin Mary, the tablets of the law contained within her symbolize our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

👉🏾The ark was made of acacia wood, a sign of the purity of the Mother of God.

✍🏾It was covered with pure gold, both inside and out, showing her holiness and purity in conscience and body. When the Israelites carried the Ark of Zion before them, they overcame all who opposed them.

✍🏾The Ark Among the Philistines

The Philistines rose up against Israel for war and gathered together to fight. The Israelites were defeated, and the ark of the covenant was taken. The elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring back the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, that it may go before us and save us from the hand of our enemies.” But the children of Israel had sinned, and God delivered the ark into the hands of the Philistines. (1 Samuel 4:1-11)

✍🏾 The Philistines brought the ark of the LORD into the house of Dagon and set it beside the idol. The next morning, Dagon had fallen on his face before the LORD.

✍🏾 They were astonished, yet they set Dagon back in his place, shut the door, and departed. The following morning, Dagon had fallen on his face again, and both his head and hands were broken. The hand of the LORD was heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and plagues struck them boils, rats, and a great calamity in the city.

✍🏾 The Philistines sent the ark to Ashkelon, saying, “We have taken it away.” The people of Ashkelon were greatly alarmed: “Why have you brought the ark of the God of Israel to kill us and our people?” they asked.

✍🏾 The ark remained with the Philistines for seven months. Their land suffered, plagues spread, and many people perished. Finally, they returned the ark to the house of Aminadab on the hill, where it remained for twenty years.

✍🏾 After twenty years, God delivered the Philistines into the hand of David, and he defeated them. The prophet of the LORD declared, “Arise, O Lord, into your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctuary.” David returned to Israel with the ark of the LORD, rejoicing and singing with great glory. He placed it in a tent that he had prepared for it.

✍🏾The Feast of Hidar Zion is celebrated for several reasons:

1. The prophet Zechariah saw Zion in the form of the seal of the covenant.

2. It is the day Menelik I entered Axum carrying the Ark of Zion.

3. During the reign of Queen Gudit (Yodit), after the Ark was hidden on Lake Zway, it returned to Axum.

4. Between 333–339 A.D., Kings Abraha and Atsbeha built the great church in Axum and consecrated it on this day.

For these sacred events, the Holy Orthodox Tewahedo Church honors the Virgin Mary, the living Ark of Zion, and celebrates the feast with great pomp and devotion. (Medble Tarikh, p. 152)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

2.Protecting Yourself From Sin

Just as we wash our bodies daily to preserve physical cleanliness, we must also guard the purity of our hearts every day. Repentance is not a one-time act but a continual labor. Loving God with a pure heart leaves no room for loving the passing things of this world.

This is why the Apostle James warns us:
“You adulterers! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Whoever wishes to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.” (James 4:4)

Worldly love separates us from God. Purity of heart means turning away from the world and following God wholly.

Our Lord also teaches:
“He who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; and he who loves son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me. And he who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.” (Matthew 10:37-38)

These words are addressed to those who choose to follow Him with an undivided, pure heart.

Saint Peter, whose heart was sincere, once said to the Lord:
“Behold, we have left everything and followed You. What shall we have?”
And the Lord replied:
“Truly I say to you, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of His glory, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” (Matthew 19:27-28)

Those who follow Christ with a pure heart will behold His glory and share in His kingdom.

3.Living a Life Filled With Love

When we speak of a pure heart, we mean an inner life free from sin, free from wrongdoing, free from doubt, and filled with holy love. A clean house is not defined by emptiness but by what is kept within it. In the same way, purity of heart is not only freedom from sin but the presence of genuine love.

Saint Paul teaches that love is the foundation and fulfillment of every virtue:

👉🏾“If I give all my possessions to feed the poor, and if I surrender my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.” (1 Corinthians 13:3)A pure heart, therefore, is a heart saturated with holy love.

Our Lord, when revealing the two greatest commandments, said:
“You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets.” (Matthew 22:37-40)

Dear faithful followers of the Orthodox teachings on the John's Repentance page, we greet you with the peace of God. Based on the topic above, we present to you this lesson so that you may read, learn, and be strengthened in spiritual understanding.

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets is one of the seven great fasts of the Church. It is observed every year from Hidar 15 until the eve of the Feast of the Nativity.

Duration and Purpose

The fast lasts 44 days before the Nativity. During this period, the faithful remember the fulfillment of the prophecies of the holy prophets and the completion of the 5500 years of human suffering before the coming of the Savior.

What the Prophets Foretold

When God the Father decreed the salvation of the world, the prophets spoke through the Holy Spirit concerning:

His taking on human flesh

His exile into Egypt

His baptism in the Jordan

His enlightening of the darkened world through His divine teaching

His sufferings for the salvation of mankind

His crucifixion and death

His resurrection

His ascension

His glorious second coming

Prophets from every generation proclaimed these mysteries under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

The Prophets’ Longing and Fasting

Desiring to see the fulfillment of God’s promise, the prophets prayed earnestly and fasted with strong determination. They counted the days, weeks, months, and years, waiting for the moment when God would become man for the salvation of the world. In their prayers they cried, “Stretch out Your strength; stretch out Your hand!” longing for the salvation to come.

Because the prophecies and prayers of the prophets were fulfilled through the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ, this fast is called “Tsome Nebiyat – the Fast of the Prophets.”

✍🏾Other Names of the Fast of the Prophets

Because this holy season carries many spiritual meanings, the Fast of the Prophets is known by several traditional names in the Church:

1. Adam’s Fast

Since the promise of salvation that God gave to Adam was fulfilled through the birth of Christ, this fast is also called Adam’s Fast.

2. The Preaching Fast

During this season the Church proclaims extensively the mystery of God becoming man. Because the gospel of the Incarnation is widely preached, it is called the Preaching Fast.

3. The Nativity Fast

The fast concludes on the Feast of the Nativity, when we celebrate the birth of the Savior. For this reason, it is also known as the Nativity Fast.

4. The Apostles’ Fast

The holy apostles said, “If we fast during the feast of the Resurrection, what shall we do during the feast of the Nativity?”
In remembrance of the prophets who fasted before the coming of Christ, the apostles also kept this fast. Therefore, it is called the Apostles’ Fast.

5. Philip’s Fast

The Apostle Saint Philip preached the Gospel throughout Afrakya, performing miracles and bringing many to the faith. He was martyred by those who rejected his teaching.
When his disciples prepared to bury him, they fasted and prayed for a week, asking God to return the apostle’s body to them. On the third day, God granted their request, and the disciples buried him with honor.
After receiving his body, they continued fasting until the Nativity. Because of this memory, the fast is called Philip’s Fast.

6. Mary’s Fast

After the Archangel Gabriel announced to the Holy Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of God through the Holy Spirit, she humbled herself and fasted, saying, “What shall I do, for I have conceived God whom heaven and earth cannot contain?”
For this reason, the fast is also known as Mary’s Fast.

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets and the Period of Teaching

During this fast:

The prophets fasted and prayed.

The apostles fasted and received blessings.

The Church Fathers established the tradition that we, the faithful, should also observe this fast so that we may receive blessings like them.

✍🏾 The Season of Teaching(Astemhro)

According to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, the period from Hidar 6 to Tahisas 7or 13) is called the period of teaching (Astemhro).

Astemhro :(when it writes with the  letter “ሀ”,in Amharic alphabet ) means the time of teaching the period when the Gospel and the goodness of God are preached widely.

The root of the word is:

Mehare – taught, gave instruction, led, showed, advised.

Temhire – learned, taught.
This signifies a time when God’s goodness, compassion, patience, and saving work are widely proclaimed in the Church.

Astemhro (when it writes with “ሐ”in Amharic alphabet) also means a time of mercy and forgiveness.

The root:

Mehare – forgave, forgave a debt.

Amhare –  to please, to forgive, to show pity, to grieve.

This is a Ge’ez verb expressing acts of mercy, compassion, and intercession, showing how one responds to the needs and sufferings of others.

The period of teaching is a time when God instructs us about His goodness and mercy. He teaches that:He forgives all our sins.We, the faithful, should also forgive one another.

✍🏾Saint Paul taught the same truth when he wrote, “For since the creation of the world, His invisible attributes, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through the things that have been made” (Romans 1:20).

By reflecting on creation, our hearts perceive the invisible God through His visible works.

Creation is therefore not merely the background of human life; it is a revelation that allows the pure heart to see God’s power, His providence, and His glory.

✍🏾Seeing God through Vision

Many holy people in Scripture saw God in visions and heard His voice, demonstrating that God reveals Himself to those who are pure in heart.

👉🏾 Hearing God’s Call

When the sons of Eli sinned against God, He called Samuel, who was pure in heart. The Scripture says:

“And the Lord came and stood, and Samuel called as at other times, Samuel: and Samuel said, ‘Speak; for thy servant heareth.’” (1 Samuel 3:1-14)

Saul also heard the voice of God on the road to Damascus:

Those who were with Saul saw the light but did not hear the voice, showing that hearing God’s call requires spiritual attentiveness.

✍🏾Seeing God in Trials

David, the noble king and servant of God, testified to God’s help in trials:

 “All my bones say to you, O Lord, who is like you? You deliver the poor from the hand of him who oppresses, the needy and the poor from the hand that snatches them away.” (Psalm 35:10)

He also declared:

 “I saw the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand, that I should not be shaken.” (Acts 2:25)

This teaches us that God is always present before the pure in heart. In trials and temptations, those with pure hearts will see

✍🏾The Division of Time during the Fast of the Prophets

According to the tradition of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church:

👉🏾Hidar 6 – Tahsas 7 or 13:
Zemene Astemhhro (Season of Instruction)

👉🏾Hidar 13 – Hidar 19:
Kidist (Holy Week)

👉🏾Hidar 20 – Hidar 26:
Mikurab (Synagogue Week)

👉🏾Hidar 27 – Tahsas 3:
Metsagu

👉🏾Tahsas 4 – Tahsas 6:
Debre Zeyt (three days only)

👉🏾Tahsas 7 – Tahsas 13:
Zemene Sibket

👉🏾Tahsas 14 – Tahsas 20:
Zemene Birhan (Season of Light)

👉🏾Tahsas 21 – Tahsas 27:
Zemene Nolawi (Season of the Shepherds)

👉🏾Tahsas 28 – Tahsas 29:
Lidet (Nativity Days)

✍🏾Meaning of Zemene Astemhro

It is a season set apart to instruct the faithful about the goodness and mercy of God, who forgives all our sins. During this time, believers are reminded that, just as God shows compassion toward us, we are called to forgive one another.

✍🏾Purpose of the Season of Astemhro

During this period:

The Church continually asks God for forgiveness on behalf of her children.

Believers repent and seek forgiveness for their sins.

Teaching is given abundantly, guiding the faithful toward spiritual renewal.

✍🏾The Sabbaths of the Season of Instruction

According to the writings of St. Yared, the Sundays of this season are:

1. Astemhro (E-tezekiro)

2. Astemhrot (Lotu Sbhat)

3. Mkurab (Synagogue – “God is perfect in His existence”)

4. Metsagu (Yibelu Israel)

5. Debre Zeyt (The Sabbath given for the rest of humankind)

These divisions were established by St. Yared in Dǝgwa Ze-Astemhro.The names of the four Sundays, except the first Astemhro , are the same as the Sundays of the Great Lent.

✍🏾Are the Sundays the Same as the Sundays of Lent(abiy tsom)?

The names of the Sundays match those of the Lenten season.
However, the content is different.

During the nights and services of these weeks:

the Psalms chanted,

the readings appointed for the Divine Liturgy, and

the teachings delivered

all differ in focus and mystery.

✍🏾Meaning of “Different in Mystery”

When we say that the teachings “differ in mystery,” we mean that their spiritual emphasis matches the appointed time.
However, the Church always teaches one unchanging foundation:

The eternal Word of God is proclaimed in every season.
