✍🏾by attaining the Stages of Holiness to see the Holy Trinity

The Holy Church teaches that the path to holiness and the vision of the Holy Trinity is cultivated through ten virtues. These virtues are grouped into three major stages of purification and spiritual growth.

1. The Purity of the Flesh ( ንፅሐ ሥጋ)

This first stage focuses on disciplining the body and the senses so that they become instruments of righteousness. It includes three forms of purity:

a. Purity of the Flesh – Mearge Tsmawe (መዓርገ ጽማዌ)

This means guarding the senses, refusing to imitate the desires of the world, and listening only to the word of God with a humble and obedient heart.

b. Purity of the Heart – Mearge Libawe (መዓርገ ልባዌ)

This is the willingness to receive the word of God deeply, storing understanding and spiritual knowledge like precious treasure.

c. Purity of the Sweet Song – Mearge Tea‘me Zimare (መዓርገ ጣዕመ ዝማሬ)

This is the devotion of praising God day and night, imitating the ceaseless hymns of the holy angels.

2. The Purity of the Soul (ንፅሐ ነፍስ)

This second stage concerns the inner transformation of the soul, cultivating four spiritual dispositions:

a. Mearge Anb'e (መዓርገ አንብዕ)

Deep reflection Crying on the sacrifice of Christ and the sins of humanity, allowing the heart to be humbled and grateful.

b. Mearge Kunene (መዓርገ ኲነኔ)

The subduing of fleshly desires so that the will of the soul may govern and lead according to righteousness.

c. Mearge Fiqir (መዓርገ ፍቅር)

The cultivation of perfect love: loving God first and loving all people sincerely and without hypocrisy.

d. Mearge Huset (መዓርገ ሁሰት)

It includes the spiritual ability to be present in  wherever one is, shining like sunlight, and to perceive what is happening in another place while remaining in one place.

3. The Purification of the Heart (ንፅሐ ልቡና)

This final and highest stage includes the mysteries granted to those who have reached spiritual maturity:

a. Mearge Nitsare Mela’ekt (መዓርገ ንፃሬ መላእክት)

The grace of seeing angels, similar to the prophets and the saints who beheld heavenly visions.

b. Immersion in the Ocean of Divine Grace, mearge Tesetmo , መዓርገ ተሰጥሞ

At this level, the soul becomes deeply united with the mercy, peace, and illumination of God.

c. Mearge Kewine esat (መዓርገ ከዊነ እሳት )

The state in which the body is surrounded by divine light, shining from head to toe like fire, as witnessed in the lives of holy men and women.

Netsrote Silus Kidus (ነጽሮተ ሥሉስ ቅዱስ)

The attainment of the seeing of the Holy Trinity. Those who reach this stage behold the divine mystery and join the angels in ceaseless praise.

These ten virtues describe the spiritual ladder that leads believers from bodily discipline, to the purification of the soul, and finally to the illumination of the heart. At the highest stage, the saints see God and praise Him together with the heavenly hosts.

✍🏾In The Second Coming of the Lord 

The Holy Church teaches that on the Last Day, when our Lord comes in His majesty to judge the living and the dead, every human being will behold Him. Saint John the Evangelist describes this awe-inspiring moment in the Revelation:

“Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, even those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth will wail because of Him.”
Revelation 1:7

Even those who crucified Him, long buried, will rise and see Him.  the Prophet Hosea described the terror of the unrepentant on that day:

“They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us,’ and to the hills, ‘Fall on us.’”Hosea 10:8

This is the fear of those who rejected God’s mercy. Scripture does not soften the reality. It tells us plainly:

“It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.”
Hebrews 10:31

When humanity stands before the throne of judgment, nothing will be hidden. All will see God, though not all will rejoice.

For the faithfuls , the Final Day is not terror but fulfillment. Saint Paul teaches the mystery of spiritual sight:

2 Corinthians 3:17-18

What the righteous taste now through the Holy Spirit, they will behold clearly after the Resurrection. Their vision is not fear but light. Their transformation begins now and completes then.

Matthew 22:30

Those who lived in faith, repentance, and love will be filled with clarity, holiness, and the joy of the Kingdom forever. Their sight of God will be eternal praise, not judgment.

✍🏾Who Are the People to Whom God Has Revealed Himself?

The Church teaches that no human being has ever seen God in His divine essence, for the Godhead is invisible, incomprehensible, and beyond all created perception. Yet, in His love, God has revealed Himself to humanity in different ways.

Saint John declares:
“No one has ever seen God; the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known.”
(John 1:18)

The revelation of God is therefore known fully in the Incarnation, when the Son of God became man for our salvation.

✍🏾Christ Revealed God to Humanity

Through the Incarnation, our Lord Jesus Christ revealed the Father to us. The apostles, who walked with Him in purity of heart, received this grace.

4. Metsagu

The fourth week of the Fast, covering the days from Hidar 27 to Tahsas 7, is called Metsagu, meaning “a sick or bedridden person.”

✍🏾Why the Day Is Called Metsagu

It commemorates the day when Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ opened the eyes of the man who was born blind, revealing His divine power and mercy.

👉🏾Hymn of the Day (Sunday)

The hymn composed by Saint Yared begins with:
“Yebelu Israel…”(“The people of Israel said, ‘We have neither seen nor heard of the man who was born blind and whose eyes were opened on the Sabbath)
It recounts the disbelief of the Israelites who said they had never seen or heard of a miracle such as the healing of the man born blind.

👉🏾Psalm of the Day

Psalm 4:2–3
"O sons of men, how long will you remain in darkness? Why do you love vanity, and why do you seek falsehood? Know that God is revealed in His righteousness.”
This psalm teaches us to recognize and believe in the wondrous works God performs for His faithful ones.

👉🏾Gospel Reading

John 9:1to the end.
The Gospel narrates the healing of the young man who was born blind. Through this miracle, Christ reveals His divine authority to heal both physical afflictions and the sicknesses of the soul. The Liturgy of the day is the Mass of God.

✍🏾Spiritual Meaning of the Week

During this week, we reflect on both the healing of the body through Christ’s miracles and the healing of the soul through His teachings.

Many people today suffer not only from physical illnesses but from spiritual blindness that keeps them from seeing the light of righteousness. These diseases include:

👉🏾Gossip

👉🏾Heresy

👉🏾Hatred

👉🏾Violence

👉🏾Theft

👉🏾Lying

👉🏾Adultery

👉🏾Immorality of all forms

👉🏾Corruption, even among those entrusted with sacred duties

These sins are deeper wounds than any bodily disease.

✍🏾The True Cure

Physical illnesses may be healed by holy water or medicine. But the sickness of sin has only one remedy: repentance.
Every person afflicted by these spiritual diseases is called to return to our Lord Jesus Christ, the eternal Healer of both body and soul.

5. Debre Zeyt

The fifth and final week of the Fast is known as Debre Zeyt, covering Tahsas 4 to 6.

Hymn of the Day (Sunday)

The hymn for this week is:
“Ser'a Senbete le-seb’e…”(“God created the Sabbath as a day of rest for all creatures in heaven and on earth.”)It praises God who established the Sabbath for all creatures in heaven and on earth.

👉🏾Psalm of the Day

Psalm 131:15–16
"I will bless her widows, I will satisfy her poor with bread, I will clothe her priests with peace, and her righteous ones will rejoice greatly."
This psalm proclaims God’s care for His Church and His people.

Luke 12:32–41
Christ teaches that since no one knows the hour of their death or the passing of the world, every Christian must live in constant spiritual readiness and Instead of gathering perishable wealth, we must increase righteous deeds that prepare the soul for the Kingdom of God.

✍🏾The Season of Sermon(Zemene sibket)

The period from Tahsas 7 to Tahsas 26 during the Fast of the Prophets is known as the Season of Sermon.

Why It Is Called the Season of Sermon(Zemene sibket)

It receives this name because during this time the Prophets foretold, taught, and proclaimed the coming of the Lord in the flesh.As the Church remembers their testimony and continues to proclaim the mystery of the Incarnation, this period is called the Season of Sermon, meaning a time of proclamation and divine teaching.

1. The First Sunday Called “Sermon”

The first Sunday of the Season of Sermon is itself called “Sermon.”(Sibket)

Meaning of the Day

On this Sabbath, the Church teaches that the Incarnation of Christ was revealed beforehand in the Torah of Moses, in the writings of the Prophets, and in the Psalms.

Because the prophets proclaimed His coming long in advance, this day is named “Sermon,” which signifies a message that unites humanity with God.

During this week the Church reflects on the genealogy of Christ, from the calling of Abraham to the kingdom of David, recognizing the prophetic preparation for the birth of the Savior.

2. The Sermon of the Prophets

On the Sabbath of Sermons, the Gospel reading declares that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is the One about whom Moses and the Prophets wrote.

Gospel Reading

(John 1:45)This part affirms that Christ is the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets.

Teachings of the Prophets

David the Prophet and King, through the Holy Spirit, foresaw and sang about the salvation brought by Christ.(“Send forth Your hand from above and save me.”)

Isaiah the Prophet, one of the greatest among them, proclaimed the mystery of the Incarnation, saying:
“Oh, that You would rend the heavens and come down, so that the mountains might shake at Your presence!” (Isaiah 64:1)
The Church teaches this prophecy as pointing to Christ descending from heaven and being born of the Virgin Mary.

3. The Preaching of the Church

Following the apostolic teaching, the Church preaches Christ at all times.

Apostolic Witness

Saint Paul teaches:
“We preach Christ crucified.” (2 Corinthians 4:5)
The Church proclaims the hope of salvation that our Lord Jesus Christ granted and accomplished for humanity.

The Hymn of Saint Yared

As Saint Yared sings,
“We preach the Son who existed before the world, who is the Savior.”
The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church continually proclaims Christ the Son of God, who died for our sins and rose to give life to all, whether in times of abundance or in times of hardship, in every season and circumstance.

Genesis 18:1–15

At the heat of the day, while Abraham sat at the door of his tent in the plains of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him. When he lifted his eyes, he saw three men standing nearby. Recognizing the divine presence, he ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed himself to the ground in deep reverence.

 Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life has been preserved.”and named the place Peniel(Genesis 32:30)

They desired to see the Savior,

“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.” (Matthew 5:9)

Peace means tranquility, calmness, rest, and contentment.
It refers to a right and holy relationship with God, oneself, and other people, founded on:

• Love
• Unity
• Harmony

Gideon declared, “The Lord is Peace” (Judges 6:24), teaching that God Himself is the source of peace. God is truly a God of peace.

Peace is one of the Fruits of the Holy Spirit, and its foundation is love (Galatians 5:22).

The Holy Gospel is called the “Gospel of Peace” because it is the message of reconciliation that God sent to humanity, and which our Lord Jesus Christ preached to the whole world (Acts 10:36; Ephesians 6:15).

Peacemakers are the living fruits of the Gospel, beloved by God.
They actively work to establish peace:

• Between human beings and God
• Between God who dwells in the heart and the inner life of a person
• Between the soul and the body

✍🏾Peacemakers as Ministers of Reconciliation

(2 Corinthians 5:18–20 )
Active peacemakers establish peace between people and God by first reconciling themselves with God. Through repentance, confession, prayer, and obedience, they become vessels of peace.

After making peace with God, they help others to become steadfast in faith, to repent, and to return to God.

👉🏾The Apostle Paul teaches:

“All things are of God, who has reconciled us to Himself through Jesus Christ, and has given us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and has committed to us the word of reconciliation. Therefore, we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were pleading through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.”(2 Corinthians 5:18–20)

This holy work of reconciliation is also carried out through the intercessions of the saints, by which many souls are drawn back to God.

✍🏾How Peacemakers Establish Peace Among People

Peacemakers first live in peace with others themselves. A person who is not at peace with people cannot bring peace between people.

After establishing peace in their own relationships, peacemakers work to create peace among others in three ways:

👉🏾First, they do not create conflict, spread rumors, or increase misunderstandings and hatred.

👉🏾Second, they actively help to resolve the problems that cause division, anger, and hostility.

👉🏾Finally, they allow love, forgiveness, and compassion to govern relationships between people.

Peace among people can exist at different levels:

• Between individuals
• Between families
• Between communities
• Between nations

A true peacemaker does not divide people but unites them through wisdom, patience, and love.

✍🏾Peace Between the Soul and the Body

Active peacemakers establish peace between the soul and the body by listening to their conscience and refusing to let fleshly desires rule their spiritual life. When the desires of the body rise against the spirit, inner conflict appears. Peace is restored when the will of the flesh is subjected to the soul.

This spiritual discipline is strengthened through:

• Fasting
• Prayer
• Almsgiving
• Perseverance in prayer

These holy practices purify the heart and bring order between the spirit and the body.

Saint Yared (ቅዱስ ያሬድ) teaches about fasting:

“Fasting heals the wounds of the soul, destroys the desires of the flesh, and teaches humility to the young.”

Inner peace is established by trusting in God and casting all our worries upon Him (Psalm 4:8; 1 Peter 5:7). This is the foundation for becoming a true peacemaker and being called a child of God.

Through these practices, the believer lives in harmony, and the peace of God dwells within the heart.

1. Making Peace Between Man and God

The way the world pursues peace and the way Christianity teaches peace are different.

The world focuses on peace between people, achieved through:
• Building good relationships
• Resolving conflicts by scientific, cultural, or legal means
• Maintaining order and security

Christian teaching, however, emphasizes that true peace begins with a good relationship between man and God.

Peace between man and God means harmony in all aspects of this relationship:

• Creator and creature
• Father and son
• Worshipper and God
• Prayer-maker and prayer recipient
• Lawgiver and judge

This relationship was first disrupted when the Devil desired to be God, turning what should have been harmony between Creator and creature into enmity.

✍🏾Through repentance, faith, and reconciliation, peacemakers restore this divine harmony, becoming instruments of God’s peace in the world.

✍🏾The peace between man and God is founded on God’s love, but this peace was broken when man sinned. Enmity arose when man disobeyed God’s command and was expelled from Paradise (by eating the fruit of the forbidden tree), creating a barrier between humanity and God (Hebrews 9:3).

✍🏾Peace in the Old Testament (Torah System)

In the Old Testament, peace with God was symbolized and temporarily restored through sacrificial practices:

The burnt offering represented reconciliation between man and God (Leviticus 6:8–13).

The blood sacrifice was offered for God alone, symbolizing atonement for sin (Hebrews 9:22; Romans 6:23).

Although these sacrifices atoned for temporary sins, they could not fully remove the enmity between man and God (Hebrews 10:4).

The wall of enmity was ultimately broken down by our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, through His sacrificial death on the cross.

✍🏾As the Mediator of the New Covenant, God incarnate reconciled humanity to Himself, restoring the lost peace and bringing man back into true fellowship with God.

✍🏾The Apostle Paul speaks of the salvation that restores peace between man and God:

👉🏾“For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” (Romans 5:10)

He further explains:

👉🏾“But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who has made the two one, having abolished the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and having broken down in his flesh the middle wall of hostility, that he might create in himself one new man from the two, making peace, having killed the hostility, and by him reconcile both to God in one body, through the cross.” (Ephesians 2:13–16)

👉🏾This teaches that our Lord Jesus Christ is our peace, who removes the barrier of hostility between humanity and God.

Paul also affirms:

👉🏾“God was pleased for all his fullness to dwell in him, and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, by making peace through the blood of his cross.” (Colossians 1:20)

✍🏾Through the sacrifice of His blood, Christ restores harmony and establishes true peace, reconciling man with God and created the foundation for peace among people and within the soul.

“He who is the Mediator of the New Testament, the Son of God, the Son of Mary, through the shedding of His precious blood brought peace between man and God. We always thank Him Jesus Christ, the Son of God who brought peace between man and God through His blood. He is the Prince of Peace, and we pray: ‘Give us Your peace, O Prince of Peace.’”

👉🏾The holy angels also proclaimed at His birth:

“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill toward men.” (Luke 2:14)

His birth brought peace to humanity, for before Him, we lived under the curse of sin.

As Saint Paul teaches:

“Among these we all once lived in the desires of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, just as the rest.” (Ephesians 2:3)

👉🏾Saint Ephrem the Syrian teaches:“He directed our feet into the way of peace.”(Wudase maryam Zekedamit )

Through the redemption of our Lord Jesus Christ, we have been brought into this way of peace.

There was no other hope for the destruction of the wall of enmity between man and God apart from the Incarnation and redemptive work of Christ.

Our Lord Himself said:

👉🏾“Righteous Father, the world has not known You, but I have known You; and these have known that You sent Me. And I have declared to them Your name, and will declare it, that the love with which You loved Me may be in them, and I in them.

✍🏾The Peace That Comes From God

The Apostle James teaches:
“Let him who turns a sinner from the error of his way know that he will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.” (James 5:20)

To turn a sinner from sin through repentance is to create peace between man and God. For this reason, God is rightly called the God of Peace
(Romans 15:33; Philippians 4:9; Hebrews 13:20).

The peace given by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is not like the peace of the world.
He said:

“Peace I leave with you, My peace I give unto you; not as the world gives, do I give unto you.” (John 14:27)

The peace of Christ is an inner peace that no one can steal.
It is peace with God and peace with others that remains firm even in trials.

Saint Paul teaches:

“The peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:7)

✍🏾Making Peace Between the Holy Scriptures and Their Interpretation

👉🏾Saint Cyril of Alexandria teaches that the words of our Lord, “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God,” also apply to those who bring peace within the understanding of the Holy Scriptures. A peacemaker is not only someone who reconciles people, but also someone who brings harmony to the interpretation of God’s word.

✍🏾Those who labor to unite the teachings of the Law and the Prophets, the Old Testament and the New Testament, the four Holy Gospels, and the Epistles are blessed. These scholars act as mediators, revealing the mystery that binds all the Scriptures together. By showing how each part completes the other, they build peace within the Church’s understanding and guard the unity of faith.

✍🏾The holy fathers who gathered at the Councils of Nicaea, Constantinople, and Ephesus are also true peacemakers. They reconciled differing interpretations, defended the Orthodox faith, and guided the Church to a unified confession. Through their spiritual labor, they protected the faithful from division and preserved the right understanding of the Scriptures.

✍🏾Blessed also are those who bring together believers who differ in reading or emphasis, helping them discover the deeper unity found in the mystery of the Scriptures. By guiding them toward agreement on what is shared and charity in what differs, they allow the Church to live in harmony.

They are called children of God because, in their work, they imitate the life of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who reconciled all things to Himself and brought peace through truth.

To be called a child of God is a great privilege. Just as a son is an heir, so too are the children of God heirs of His promises (Romans 8:17).

👉🏾The Evangelist Saint John says:
"But as many as received Him, to them He gave power to become children of God, even to those who believe in His name; who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God" (John 1:12-13).

"Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God; and everyone who loves the Father loves Him who is born of Him. By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep His commandments" (1 John 5:1-2).

✍🏾The promise that God has given to His children is that they will be set free from the bondage of corruption and will attain the glorious freedom of the children of God (Romans 8:21).

If children, then heirs; heirs of God; if indeed we suffer with Him, then we are joint heirs with Christ, so that we may also be glorified together" (Romans 8:14-17).

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

The Feast of Be’ata Le-Maryam, celebrated on the third day of Tahsas ,is one of the thirty-three feasts of the Holy Virgin. In Gë`ëz, the name refers to the commemoration of the day when Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, was brought into the temple.

✍🏾The Prayer and Vow of Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah

The parents of Our Lady, Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah, lived many years without a child. Infertility in those days was regarded as a great shame, and those considered barren were often excluded from joining the faithful in the temple. Even so:

Their love for one another never diminished.

They never forgot God for even a single day.

They waited with hope for His work to be revealed.

They continually vowed to give back the child God would grant them.

God heard their sincere prayers, and in His mercy He gave them a daughter: the Holy Virgin Mary. Though she was their child for a time, she was ultimately given for the salvation of Adam and all creation.

✍🏾The Childhood of the Holy Virgin

The psalmist David says, “I will go into Your house with burnt offerings; I will pay You the vows my lips have spoken in my distress” (Psalm 65:12). In the same spirit, Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah went to the temple to fulfill the vows they had made. God heard their prayer and granted them a child, and they, in turn, offered that child back to Him. This reflects the pattern found in the Torah, where Hannah, the mother of the prophet Samuel, having suffered greatly because of her barrenness, vowed that if God granted her a son, she would dedicate him to the house of the Lord. God answered her prayer, and she faithfully brought Samuel to serve before Him (1 Samuel 1:22–28).

These noble and righteous parents, chosen to become the ancestors of the Sun of Righteousness, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, likewise dedicated their three-year-old daughter, the Holy Virgin Mary, to God. They went to the priest Zechariah, explained the vow they had made, and entrusted their blessed child into his care.

✍🏾The Heavenly Provision for the Virgin

“When the priest Zechariah became concerned about the food of the Virgin, he entrusted the matter to God. In response, God sent the holy archangel Saint Phanuel, one of the most glorious angels, to provide for her. As recorded in the Book of Enoch, Phanuel is described as:

“The fourth of the glorious archangels, appointed over those who repent, to be the hope of those who will inherit eternal life.”
(Enoch 10:8–15)

This same angel, by God’s wisdom and will, was appointed as the heavenly steward of the Mother of the Lord. He served her with complete faithfulness.

The Psalmist testifies, “He gave the bread of angels to eat” (Psalm 77:25). In this way, the Holy Virgin lived in the temple nourished by heavenly bread and a heavenly cup, provided through the hand of an angel. It is called heavenly bread and a heavenly cup because it was received from above and given by divine grace.

Likewise, in the Torah, the people of Israel lived on manna that came down from heaven (Exodus 16:10–13). The Scriptures also record that the prophet Elijah was strengthened for forty days by food given to him by an angel (1 Kings 19:9).

In the same manner, Our Lady lived in the temple under the protection of angels, guarded, nourished, and preserved by their ministry.

✍🏾The Holy Virgin as the True Ark of the Covenant

For the Lord has chosen Zion; He has desired her for His dwelling place:‘This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.’”(Psalm 131:14)

The entrance of the Virgin Mary into the temple signifies the entrance of the true Ark of the Covenant into the earthly sanctuary. The ancient ark was a symbol of the true and living Ark, Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary.

In the first temple, beyond the second veil, was the Holy of Holies. This sacred place is a symbol of the heart of Our Lady, the true Holy of Holies, the image of her pure body and soul. The ark within it was covered with gold and held the golden pot of manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant (Hebrews 9:3–4).

Our Lady is pure in spirit, soul, and body, shining with the holiness of pure gold in every aspect of her being.

Within her womb was found the true manna, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, announced by the angel. Just as Aaron’s rod blossomed without being planted or watered, the Holy Virgin conceived without seed. Her womb remained virgin, and the seal of her purity was unbroken, revealing the mystery of how she became the Mother of God without corruption.

The first temple was a model of Our Lady, and the ancient ark foreshadowed her. She, the Ark of Faith, entered the earthly temple on Tahsas 3; and now she dwells eternally in the temple of heaven, the kingdom of God, which is her everlasting resting place (Psalm 131:13–14).

May the intercession, love, tenderness, and motherly care of the Holy Virgin Mary be with us forever. May her prayers strengthen us as we strive to walk in purity and faith, just as she was preserved in holiness from her youth.


May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

✍🏾 His Birth and Early Life

Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus was born in the land of Nehisa (Egypt). His father’s name was Simeon, and his mother’s name was Aklesia. They lived without children for thirty years and grieved greatly.

One day, Aklesia entered the temple of God, fell before the Holy Trinity, and prayed with tears, asking God to grant her a son whose glory would surpass earthly honor and belong to heaven. God accepted her prayer. She conceived on Megabit 29 and gave birth on Tahsas 29.

At the moment of his birth, the child stood up and glorified God, saying:

“Glory to the Father, glory to the Son, and glory to the Holy Spirit, who has come into the world as the Light of the world.”

Peacemaking reflects the heart of God. The noble prophet David teaches us, saying:

“Seek peace and pursue it.”
(Psalm 34:14)

Even in our time, there are faithful fathers, mothers, sons, and daughters who pray for peace and strive to live in peace. For this, we give thanks to God. However, it is deeply painful to witness the rise of criticism, bullying, and insults, especially on social media. These behaviors, born of selfishness and lack of love for others, have widened the divisions among us.

Instead of working to live together in peace, many have come to believe that “it is better to separate than to remain united.” More troubling still is that some who claim to represent the Church, and who speak in the name of the Church, have themselves become sources of division, thereby harming the peace of the Church.

In the religious sphere especially, we now argue over minor and unnecessary matters to the point that people say, “Going to church removes peace, but staying away gives peace.” By our lack of peace, we have caused many to distance themselves from the Church of God.

✍🏾The prophet Jeremiah rebuked such behavior when he said:

 “They say, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.”

We proclaim peace with our lips, yet our hearts are not at peace. Worse still, the Church, which prays for peace for the whole world, is increasingly seen seeking justice from secular courts, peace from police and security forces, and resolution through lawsuits. This reality is especially evident in disputes over church buildings and land, particularly in Western countries.

After the Church was built as a house of worship for Christ and all Christians, we began to argue over it as “mine” and “yours,” treating it as mere property. How can God accept our prayers when we force brothers and sisters, born of the same Father, to leave the Church in order to pray?

Our Lord clearly commanded us:

“First be reconciled to your brother.”(Matthew 5:24)

✍🏾Division Among Brothers

Throughout history, heretics and false teachers caused suffering within the Church. But in our time, something even more painful has appeared: brother labeling brother, persecuting one another, and praising those who destroy peace as heroes or patriots.

How can peace grow when division is celebrated? How can it be considered a victory when brothers leave the Church? Let us remember how the early Fathers mourned when Arius departed from the Church, saying with tears:

 “It is like cutting off a part of the body.”

The Fathers also taught that those of other denominations can only return to the Mother Church through love, patience, and teaching, not through hostility. How then can we preach peace while delivering sermons that make others see us as enemies and push them further away?

✍🏾True Christian Peace

According to Christian teaching, peace is not achieved by destroying or silencing one side, but by living together in love. Our fathers taught that peace is built through love, and this love is revealed in Jesus Christ, the God of peace.

“They do not know the way of peace.”(Romans 3:17)

We have wasted much time in arguments, turning even the Church into a place of conflict. While doing so, when do we find time to serve peacefully? When we criticize a servant of God while he lives and praise him only after his death, this does not create peace. If we love people while they are alive, peace will grow among us.

Even if we cannot become apostles of peace like the ancient Fathers, we must at least avoid destroying peace.

Whoever receives a messenger sent by God will receive peace from God. This peace is not only for the individual but also flows outward, creating unity of spirit with others.

“Make every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.”(Ephesians 4:3)

The unity of the Spirit is sustained through peaceful worship, peaceful service, and peaceful living.

In these words, our Lord teaches that sharing in suffering for His sake being reviled, persecuted, and falsely accused is a true manifestation of the Christian life. Suffering endured for Christ is not a sign of abandonment, but a mark of faithfulness.

The Evangelist Luke also writes:

“Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you, and revile you, and cast out your name as evil, for the sake of the Son of Man. Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for indeed your reward is great in heaven; for in like manner their fathers did to the prophets.”(Luke 6:22–23)

These words show clearly that hatred, exclusion, and separation are also part of the path prepared for those who follow Christ.

👉🏾In the previous verses, our Lord had been referring to “them” in the third person, speaking from a distance in time, extending to the end of the world, and in place, to the ends of the earth. But at this point, He changes His manner of speech and addresses them directly as “you,” speaking in the second person.

✍🏾By doing so, He speaks first to the Christians who were present at the Sermon on the Mount, and at the same time to all who would later be gathered into His Holy Church. He addresses them personally as “you.” In this verse, He speaks especially of His disciples those who are reviled, persecuted, hated, excluded, and falsely accused of all kinds of evil for His name’s sake, that is, for the sake of the Son of Man.

In short, they suffer because they are Christians. This verse is a unique and powerful teaching about the suffering that will come upon the Church, and about the glory that is revealed through enduring suffering for Christ’s sake.

✍🏾In this passage, our Lord makes special mention of the holy prophets who suffered before. By this, He teaches that just as people persecuted the prophets whom God sent in earlier times, they will also persecute His disciples. God sent the prophets, and He also sent the apostles. Both the prophets and the apostles were taught that they would endure suffering for His sake and, through that suffering, enter into eternal joy.

✍🏾 Just as persecuting the prophets who were the messengers of God is truly persecuting the God who sent them, so persecuting Christians is persecuting Christ Himself. Christians are the Body of Christ, and He identifies Himself with them.

👉🏾Our Lord did not say, “Why are you persecuting Christians?”
He said, “Why are you persecuting Me?”

Therefore, persecuting Christians is persecuting Christ Himself.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it

✍🏾“If You Know These Things and Do Them, You Are Blessed”

The early Church Fathers, after explaining the nine Beatitudes recorded in the Gospel of Matthew, taught that a tenth beatitude would be revealed through the Gospel of John. Later, while explaining the words of our Lord in John 13:17, they said, “This is the beatitude we spoke of, which John brings.”

The focus of this lesson is imitating our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ by following the example He gave us. Just as He served others, we are called to serve one another. Those who know this teaching and practice it are truly called blessed.

✍🏾The Foundation of the Tenth Beatitude

The foundation of this beatitude is found in the event of Holy Thursday, when our Lord Jesus Christ washed the feet of His apostles.

Saint John the Evangelist writes:
“So when He had washed their feet, taken His garments, and sat down again, He said to them, ‘Do you know what I have done to you? You call Me Teacher and Lord, and you say well, for so I am. If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you. Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is he who is sent greater than he who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.’”(John 13:12–17)


Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ became man in the flesh for our redemption and as an example for us to follow. By His incarnation and His sacrifice on the Cross, He broke down the wall of separation and hostility between God and humanity, offering Himself as a ransom for our salvation. At the same time, He presented Himself as a living example, saying in effect, “Do likewise.”

In this way, Christ became the perfect model for us to imitate. This is the mystery of Christ-likeness that the Apostle Saint Paul taught when he said:
“Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ.”(1 Corinthians 11:1)

This beloved Apostle also wrote to his disciple Timothy, saying:

👉🏾 Why did the Church judge that the priest should receive and then leave to be disciplined?

✍🏾 Why was the priest allowed to continue serving and distributing Holy Communion after laughing? Because from inside the sanctuary no one can see that the priest laughed, and if he were sent out without receiving Holy Communion, it could cause confusion and doubt among the faithful.

✍🏾When the faithful see a priest leaving the Mass in the middle of the Holy Liturgy, they may begin to question the Holy Sacrifice, saying,“What did the priest see in the sacrifice?”This can cause confusion and doubt among the faithful.

✍🏾 But a believer should not say or do anything that is not acceptable in the holy temple. Since everyone can see him when he laughs, it may become a source of distraction and irritation to others.. Therefore, to preserve reverence in the church, he must leave immediately so that nothing inappropriate is said or done in the holy temple.

✍🏾No one should spit in the church. If a person is suffering from illness or discomfort, he should quietly receive the saliva in his handkerchief, without making any sound, and discreetly wipe it away.

✍🏾Let no one speak foolish or meaningless words in the church or during the Holy Liturgy.

The prayers offered during the Liturgy are powerful and acceptable before God.

👉🏾Unity and forgiveness

👉🏾Fasting and prayer

We receive exhortation within the Holy Liturgy.

👉🏾 For example, if a person has a quarrel with his brother, the Holy Liturgy (kidase egzi'e) teaches him to forgive. During the Holy Liturgy, the priest prays specifically for the offerings brought by the faithful. If no offering is brought, we must ask ourselves, “For whom is this prayer offered?”

The sense of smell is sanctified through the fragrance of incense, which symbolizes the prayers of the saints rising to God.

👉🏾 The Tongue (Taste):

The tongue is sanctified when the faithful receive Holy Communion with reverence and faith.

👉🏾 Touch:

The sense of touch is sanctified when we bow before God, kiss the Holy Gospel after its reading, and receive blessings by kissing the priest’s hand at the conclusion of the Holy Liturgy.

👉🏾The Universal Epistles

👉🏾The Psalms of David

👉🏾Therefore, the Holy Liturgy  must be celebrated in the presence of the Church.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today,based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it

✍🏾We celebrate the Holy Liturgy because our Lord Jesus Christ said:

👉🏾“Where two or three are gathered together in My name, there I am in the midst of them.”
(Matthew 18:20)

✍🏾Our gathering together,founded on the eternal promise of our Lord, becomes the means through which we receive His grace and divine help.

✍🏾Just as the Holy Liturgy is the true image of the one Heavenly Church, the gathering of believers is the first and essential foundation of the Holy Liturgy.

✍🏾The liturgical order that is fulfilled in the Holy Liturgy first existed in the world of the holy angels.On earth, this same heavenly order is fulfilled when the faithful gather together in the temple of God.(Isaiah 6:1)

✍🏾We now reflect on the deep reverence and spiritual understanding with which the ancient Church,in the time of the apostles, regarded the gathering of believers.Through faithful obedience to the word of the Lord, the Church received its order of worship from the heavenly hosts, and this sacred order of thanksgiving was handed down through Holy Tradition, becoming the foundation of the life of the Church.

✍🏾The Ancient Tradition of Gathering Believers in the Holy Liturgy

✍🏾The practice of gathering together to glorify God and offer sacrifice is already found in the Old Testament. However, the true foundation of the Christian Holy Liturgy was established when our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ celebrated the Passover with His disciples on the night before His suffering.(Luke 22:7)

✍🏾Just as God chose the sons of Jacob as the foundation of the congregation of Israel, Christ gathered the apostles and made them the foundation of the Church. He seated them at the table of the Kingdom of Heaven, forming the new assembly of believers, the true Israel.
(Luke 22:29–30)

✍🏾Through this act, the unity of the Church was established in and through the apostles. Having received understanding of the divine mysteries through the grace of the Holy Spirit, the apostles gathered the faithful and celebrated the Holy Liturgy together as one body.(Acts 20:7)

✍🏾This practice was firmly rooted in the apostolic Church.The Apostle Paul clearly speaks of believers coming together as a necessary condition for worship, saying:

👉🏾“When you come together as a church…”(1Corinthians 11:18)
He further explains that this order was not human invention, but divine tradition:

👉🏾“For I received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you.”
(1Corinthians 11:23)

✍🏾This reveals the mystery of the gathering of believers in the Holy Liturgy, a sacred practice that has been preserved and handed down through Holy Tradition as an essential part of the life of the Church.

✍🏾The Fathers of the Church, who were disciples and successors of the apostles, faithfully received this apostolic tradition and handed it down directly to the generations that followed. They confirmed its truth by teaching that the faith of the Church and the Holy Liturgy are inseparable, for the teaching of the Church is expressed in the Liturgy, and the Liturgy, in turn, proclaims and confirms the teaching of the Church.

✍🏾During the time of these apostolic Fathers, all believers took part in the Holy Liturgy and approached the Holy Mysteries. Even those who were sick were not excluded, but were brought so that they might receive and share in the grace of the Liturgy.

✍🏾Anyone who deliberately missed the Holy Liturgy without illness or serious reason was regarded as having separated himself from the life of the Church.For this reason, church buildings were constructed to accommodate the full celebration of the Holy Mysteries and the participation of the entire community. This ancient understanding of church architecture continues to be clearly seen in our Church today.

✍🏾The structure and practice of the Holy Liturgy clearly show that every prayer offered by the priest and every proclamation made by the deacon are completed through the response of the faithful, who affirm them with “Amen.” The instructions found in the Metshafe kidase, which say, “Say, priest; say, deacon; say, people,” bear witness to this shared participation.

✍🏾Through this, we understand that the Holy Liturgy is a mystery of unity. It does not belong to the clergy alone, but is celebrated together by both the clergy and the faithful as one body. For this reason, the ancient instruction reminds us that the Holy Liturgy should not begin until the faithful are gathered, so that this unity may be fully expressed.

✍🏾The idea that the Holy Liturgy belongs only to priests, while the faithful are merely observers, is foreign to the life and order of the Church. Such thinking is a serious misunderstanding. The Holy Liturgy is not a performance to be watched, but a prayer of communion shared by the whole Church.

✍🏾The lack of active participation that is sometimes seen today, and the spiritual weakness that follows, arise from this misunderstanding. Since the Holy Liturgy is the communion of Christians, every Orthodox believer has the responsibility to prepare himself, to sanctify himself, and to participate fully in the life of the Church through the Liturgy.

✍🏾 Abune Tekle Haymanot, of Bulga Debre Tslalsh, also known as Zorere St. Michael Church , was conceived on Megabit 24 by his father, the priest Tsega Zeab, and his mother, the holy woman Egzi Hareya. He was born on Tahsas 24, 1197 AD, and was given the name Fisha Zion, which means the joy of Zion.

✍🏾On the third day after his birth, he descended from his mother’s arms and praised the Holy Trinity, saying, “One Father, one Son, one Holy Spirit.”He died on Nehase 24.

✍🏾 “Tekil” means a fruitful tree, a spice, a leaf, an edible and fragrant herbaceous plant, as well as a law or a system.(Matthew 15:13)

✍🏾 “Religion(haymanot)” means believing and testifying in the power of God, that God is the Creator of all, believing in the unity and Trinity of God, and in the succession of saints.

✍🏾 The phrase “Tekile Haymanot” means a plant of religion: a tree that bears the fruit of righteousness, a tree that escapes the heat of sin, a spice that delights believers with the word of the Gospel, a leaf that gives life, a leaf that satisfies the hunger of the soul when eaten, and a plant that is a shelter for the righteous.

“Tekle Haymanot” means the plant of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This name explains the spiritual identity of the righteous man.

✍🏾 By the grace and guidance of his father, the priest tsega Zeab, he studied the Church’s teachings and order. At the age of fifteen, he received the ordination of deacon from the Archbishop of Alexandria, Abune Kerlos (Gerlos). In this way, he served the Holy Church from his youth.

✍🏾 One day, while the righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot was hunting with his friends, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ appeared to him and chose him as a new apostle for Ethiopian Christians. He was given the name Tekle Haymanot, which means the fruit of faith.

✍🏾 When our father began his apostolic journey, he said:
“O Lord Jesus Christ! Behold, I have left my house open for You, that You may open the door of the Kingdom of Heaven to me.
For me who am weak, there is no one to comfort me without You.
For me who am confused, there is no one to lift me up without You.
For me who am sad, there is no one to comfort me without You.
For me who am poor, I have no refuge without You.”(Gedle Tekle Haymanot, Chapter 28, Verses 2–3)

✍🏾After saying this, with a humble and broken heart, he prayed to his Creator and preached in different regions of Ethiopia, turning people:

👉🏾 From sin to active righteousness

👉🏾 From apostasy to faith

Because of this, he was called the light of the sun for Ethiopians.

✍🏾In his Letter to the Hebrews, Saint Paul describes the spiritual struggle of the saints:

👉🏾“They conquered kingdoms through faith” (Hebrews 11:33).
Likewise, our father Saint Tekle Haymanot, through spiritual struggle, humility, and miracles, converted King Motolomi, who was an unbeliever, to Christianity.

👉🏾 “They did righteousness” (Hebrews 11:33).In the same way, our father labored and struggled for the Gospel.

👉🏾 “They stopped the mouths of lions” (Hebrews 11:33).Likewise, our father crushed the head of the dragon.

👉🏾“They escaped the edge of the sword” (Hebrews 11:34).Our father was miraculously saved from the spear thrown by Motolomi.

👉🏾“They were strengthened from weakness” (Hebrews 11:34).
Our father was strengthened in many struggles, through fasting and prayer without rest.

✍🏾While doing all these things, and when the time of his rest came, he said to his disciples:

👉🏾“My children, it does not mean that all monks will enter the Kingdom of Heaven, but only those who have truly despised the world will enter. First seek the righteousness of God, fast and pray regularly, love one another, and keep His commandments strictly.”Later, he said:

👉🏾“I am the salt of the world, I am the darkness of myself. What shall I answer when I stand before the true Judge, the Lord?”

✍🏾He prayed with complete humility and deep spiritual inspiration. Therefore, our Church teaches us to remember the righteous, to pray for the poor in their name, and to make their memorial, as it is written in Matthew 10:41–42.

The righteous saints are:

👉🏾 Those whose prayers we believe in, whether they are in the flesh or have departed from this world,

👉🏾 Those who pray to God and intercede before God,

👉🏾 Those who bring us salvation of both body and soul,

👉🏾 They are our intercessors and mediators in times of trouble.

Among these saints is the Ethiopian righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot.

✍🏾 Our father Abune Tekle Haymanot:

👉🏾 Gave his whole life to God,

👉🏾 Bound himself like an ox,

👉🏾 Armed himself like a farmer,

👉🏾 Despised this world,

👉🏾 Devoted himself to fasting and prayer,

👉🏾 Lived a life of peace.

✍🏾 In addition, like the holy apostles:

👉🏾 He preached the Gospel throughout Ethiopia,

👉🏾 In the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, he healed sick bodies through miracles,

👉🏾 He healed sick souls through his teachings.

✍🏾 Among the feasts on which Abune Tekle Haymanot is remembered, his birth is commemorated on Tahisas 24.

✍🏾 When the Book of the Sinksar speaks of his birth, it honors him with the title “the new apostle.”

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today,based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

1. The Secret of Our Gathering

The secret of our gathering in the Holy Liturgy is unity. The unity of the faithful forms the Holy Church, which is the Body of Christ. As Saint Paul teaches:

“You are the body of Christ, and individually you are body part of him.”(1 Corinthians 12:27)

✍🏾When the faithful gather, the Church is revealed not as an earthly institution or administrative body, but as a heavenly reality. This gathering is the fulfillment of the Church’s unity and holiness.

✍🏾The Church is not simply a crowd of people assembled in one place. It is the manifestation of the heavenly Body of Christ, the communion of believers who become its members through faith in His Name.

2. The Perfection and Holiness of the Church

✍🏾We must be attentive in our time, because new theological doctrines have appeared that reject many of the ancient traditions of the Church. These earthly doctrines show little concern for the Holy Liturgy, and even when they speak about it, they divide it into parts, emphasizing one while diminishing another, as if the mystery of God can be measured and ranked.

✍🏾When questioned about the Holy Liturgy, they focus almost entirely on the moment when the bread and wine are changed, while neglecting the rest of the sacred service. They attempt to explain and analyze this mystery not in the Orthodox and heavenly manner handed down by the Fathers, but through scientific, rational, and earthly reasoning.

✍🏾Such teachings are not in harmony with the Holy Scriptures nor with the Apostolic Tradition of the Church. The Holy Liturgy is not a subject for experimentation or proof, but a divine and heavenly mystery revealed through faith.

✍🏾The ancient Church, our holy Fathers, understood this deeply. Knowing that the Holy Liturgy is a participation in heaven itself, they were greatly concerned when even one believer was absent from the gathering of the faithful.

3. The Holiness of the Church Comes from Christ

The holiness of the Church does not come from the personal righteousness of its members. Each of us may be weak and sinful, yet the Church remains holy because Christ Himself is present in her.

✍🏾The unity of the faithful is the purity of the Church. This holiness is not our achievement. It is the gift of Christ, who dwells among us.

✍🏾The Church is pure not because we are without sin, but because Christ is in her midst. He is the medicine for our sickness, the source of her holiness, and the life of her body.

Thus, the Church truly deserves to be called:

👉🏾a holy nation

👉🏾a royal priesthood

👉🏾a chosen generation

As Scripture says:

👉🏾“But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation… that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.”(1 Peter 2:9)

For this reason, believers in the Apostolic age were called “saints.” They lived in constant fellowship and prayer, and as Saint Paul writes:

“I have had great joy and encouragement because of your love, for the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.”(Philemon 1:7)

4. The Gathering as a Heavenly Joy

The gathering of the faithful was a fragrance of holiness and a source of heavenly joy. This joy enabled the early Christians to endure suffering with gladness and to preach the Gospel with courage in a hostile world.

Their unity was born from the love of God, and through it, the Church shone as a living witness to Christ.

5. The Priesthood in the Holy Liturgy

✍🏾Just as the gathering of the faithful reveals the Body of Christ, the priest who presides over the Holy Liturgy reveals the Priesthood of Christ, who is the Head of the Church:

👉🏾“Christ is the Savior of the body, the Church.”(Ephesians 5:23)

✍🏾The priest serves by grace, bearing witness to the eternal priesthood of Christ. His vestments are not personal decorations; they manifest the Church as the dwelling place of Christ.

For this reason, according to the Church’s order, the priest must not wear his liturgical vestments before the faithful gather. The Liturgy is not an individual act; it belongs to the whole Body.

The crown worn by the priest testifies to the eternal priesthood of Christ:

👉🏾“You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”(Psalm 109:4; Hebrews 7:1–22)

✍🏾In this way, the eternal priesthood of our Lord is manifested among the faithful in His eternal and heavenly sanctuary, the Holy Church. When we gather together, Christ Himself is in our midst. Therefore, our gathering in the Holy Liturgy is truly great, not because of our number or worthiness, but because our Savior, Jesus Christ, is present among us.

6. Preparation for the Holy Liturgy

If Abraham was commanded to leave his land and his father’s house in obedience to God, how much more should we leave behind worldly desires when we ascend to Mount Zion, the assembly of the firstborn?(Genesis 12:1; Hebrews 12:22–24)

✍🏾 If the people of Israel prepared for three days before the revelation of God on Mount Sinai, washing their clothes and sanctifying themselves, how much more should we prepare to meet Christ Himself, who was crucified for us?

Our preparation must go beyond clean clothes. We must cleanse our hearts, bodies, flesh, and blood through repentance.
(Exodus 19:14–15)

✍🏾Our Response During the Liturgy

✍🏾When the child Samuel heard the voice of God in the temple, he responded with readiness and obedience. Likewise, we who are gathered in the true Temple, the Holy Church, must respond attentively to God’s voice spoken through Scripture, prayers, hymns, and mysteries during the Holy Liturgy.(1 Samuel 3:1–14)

After the fall, Adam lived in deep repentance. According to the teaching handed down in the Church,Adam mourned bitterly for his sin, crying and repenting for many years, saying:

For this reason, the prophet Micah foretold:

“But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for Me One who is to be ruler in Israel, whose goings forth are from of old, from everlasting.”(Micah 5:2)

✍🏾 Saint Ephrem the Syrian, in his homilies on the Nativity, speaks of the great mystery of salvation revealed on this holy day:

“A great light has dawned on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. God, who dwells among the saints, became man from a pure Virgin in order to save us. What #Sacrifices Are Offered #During the #Liturgy?

(Part 8)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

1. Meaning of the Divine Liturgy

The Divine Liturgy is a communal prayer offered in unity, according to the order of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. It is the highest and most complete form of prayer, because in it the faithful unite with heaven, the angels, and the saints.

During the Divine Liturgy, five sacrifices are offered. Every Christian who participates offers these sacrifices to God.

The Five Sacrifices Offered During the Liturgy

1. The Eucharistic Sacrifice

During the Divine Liturgy, the bread is transformed into the Body of Christ, and the wine is transformed into His Blood by the power of the Holy Spirit.
This holy sacrifice is offered only during the Liturgy. Outside the Liturgy, there is no Eucharistic sacrifice.

The holy sacrifice prepared in Bethlehem and is offered in the church, which represents Calvary. Our Lord was born in Bethlehem, where the sacrifice was prepared, and through His crucifixion on Calvary the sacrifice was completed for the salvation of the whole world. Therefore, the holy sacrifice is continually offered to the faithful in the church, which is spiritually called Calvary.

2. The Sacrifice of the Lips

This is the sacrifice of thanksgiving, praise, and prayer, offered by the priest, the deacon, and the people together.
As Scripture says, it is the fruit of our lips, offered in unity to our Creator.

3. The Sacrifice of the Lamp

The lamps lit during the Liturgy are an offering to God.

They symbolize Our Lord Jesus Christ, who came as the Light of the world, illuminating those who sit in darkness.

4. The Sacrifice of Incense

Incense is offered only by the priest. He incenses the altar, the sanctuary, and the congregation.

This symbolizes the prayers of the faithful ascending to the throne of the Holy Trinity.

Just as the angels in heaven offer incense before God while proclaiming, “Holy, Holy, Holy,” so the priest on earth represents the heavenly ministry and offers incense to God.

5. The Bodily Sacrifice

During the Liturgy, the faithful stand for most of the service.

At specific moments, they bow down and humble themselves before God.

Standing, bowing, and physical reverence are all forms of bodily sacrifice, offered in obedience and humility to the Creator.

✍🏾 The Three Main Parts of the Divine Liturgy

The Divine Liturgy is divided into three major sections:

1.The Preparation

2.The Reading and Teaching

3.fre kidase (main holy liturgy )

The Holy Liturgy here vary according to the feast day, and there are fourteen in total. These are:

1.The Holy Liturgy

2.Kidase of the Apostles

3.Kidase of Our Lord

4.Kidase of the Virgin Mary

5.Kidase of Yohannes Welde Negodgwad

6.Kidase of the Three Saints

7.Kidase of Saint Athanasius

8.Kidase of Saint Basil

9.Kidase of Saint Gregory

10.Kidase of Saint Epiphanius

11.Kidase of Saint John Afewerk

12.Kidase of Saint Cyril (Zekerlos / Qerellos)

13.Kidase of Saint Jacob the Apostle

14.Kidase of Saint Dioscorus

Each holy liturgy is chosen according to the feast, season, or saint commemorated.

👉🏾 If it is the feast of Our Lord, the Holy Liturgy is Kidase Egzi

👉🏾 During the Advent of Our Lord and if pagume is on sunday, the Holy Liturgy of Saint Athanasius is celebrated.

👉🏾If it is the feast of Our Lady, the Holy Liturgy of the Virgin Mary is celebrated
(Gosa Labye Qale Senaye).

👉🏾 If it is the feast of the angels or the apostles, the Holy Liturgy of Saint Jacob of Serugh (Jacob Zesrug) is celebrated.

👉🏾 From the Feast of the Nativity until the Feast of the Circumcision, the Holy Liturgy of Saint Gregory the Theologian is celebrated.

Number of servants in the Holy Liturgy

✍🏾The Holy Liturgy is often celebrated with five servants , symbolizing the five pillars of the holy mysteries.

However, it may also be celebrated with other numbers, each carrying spiritual meaning:

👉🏾Seven represent the seven mysteries (sacraments) of the Church

👉🏾Thirteen represent the twelve Apostles and Our Lord

👉🏾Twenty-four represent the twenty-four heavenly priests

👉🏾At minimum, the Holy Liturgy may be consecrated by one priest and one deacon, representing the union of divinity and humanity.

Three represent the Holy Trinity

Four represent the four Evangelists

If there are fewer than two ministers, even if there is only one person, the Holy Liturgy must not be consecrated , as this is forbidden by the canons of the Church.

✍🏾The Call to Prayer (“Pray”)

“Pray” is a liturgical command within the Holy Liturgy. It is proclaimed thirteen times, and four times during the third part of the Liturgy.

👉🏾When the deacon proclaims “Pray,” he turns his face toward the people and calls them to prayer.

👉🏾If there is a special offering, the appropriate prayer is said in its place.

👉🏾If there is no offering, the deacon proclaims “Abune Ze Besemayat,” and the people repeat the Lord’s Prayer.

For example:
When the deacon says, “Pray for the people who give gifts to the Church,” the prayer “Abune ZeBesemaat” is not repeated at that time.

This is because this proclamation has its own specific prayer.
The supplication “Pray for the people who give gifts to the Church” itself becomes the prayer and replaces Abune ZeBesemaat.

👉🏾 When Drget is lowered, and the deacon proclaims,

“Tseliyu be entiane”
the faithful are commanded to pray the 150th Psalm of David.
In this section, the command to pray refers specifically to Psalm 150, and not to Abune ZeBesemaat.

✍🏾 When we Christians celebrate the Holy Liturgy:

👉🏾 Forgiveness of sins is granted, because repentance is offered with a contrite conscience.

👉🏾 Blessings are received in both soul and body.

👉🏾 Prayers are heard

👉🏾Question :I wanted to ask about how religion differences in dating are thought in our teachings in detail?

👉🏾Answer : My beloved child, may God's abundant grace always illuminate your path. This is a question of immense practical and spiritual importance, touching upon the very foundation of family life and our journey towards salvation. It speaks to the wisdom of the Church, which, like a loving mother, guides her children in all aspects of their lives, especially in matters as weighty as marriage and the formation of a household.

As we discussed earlier, the Orthodox Church, in her profound wisdom and experience of millennia, holds a clear and consistent teaching on marriage, which naturally extends to the dating relationships that lead to it.

The ideal, the blessed path that the Church always encourages, is for Orthodox Christians to marry within the Orthodox faith. This is not a matter of exclusivity or judgment towards those outside our fold, but rather a deep understanding of what constitutes a truly unified spiritual life for a couple and their future family.

Let us ponder this through the lens of Holy Scripture and the teachings of our Fathers:

✍🏾The Call to Unity: "Unequally Yoked"

The foundational principle is found in the Apostle Paul's admonition: "Do not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers. For what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness? And what communion has light with darkness? And what accord has Christ with Belial? Or what part has a believer with an unbeliever?" (2 Corinthians 6:14-15, )

While this passage speaks broadly to various associations, its application to marriage, the most intimate and foundational of human unions, is profound and undeniable. When a farmer yokes two animals together, they must be of the same strength and nature to plow a straight furrow effectively. If they are unequal, the plow will veer off course, and the burden will fall unevenly, causing stress and imbalance.

✍🏾Why is this Unity So Crucial in Marriage?

1.  The Home as a "Small Church": In the Orthodox understanding, the Christian home is not merely a secular dwelling; it is meant to be a "domestic church," a living cell of the Body of Christ. The husband and wife, united in the Mystery of Holy Matrimony, are called to grow together in holiness, to pray together, to fast together, to partake of the Holy Sacraments together, and to raise their children in the fear and love of God. This shared spiritual vision and practice are exceedingly difficult, if not impossible, when spouses come from different spiritual traditions or lack a shared faith in Christ.

2.  Shared Spiritual Destination: For the Orthodox Christian, the ultimate goal of life is theosis – deification, union with God. Marriage is a path to salvation, a means by which two souls help each other to attain this blessed end. If one spouse is striving towards this through the Orthodox Sacraments, ascetical life, and theological understanding, while the other holds a different path, their ultimate spiritual destinations, and the means to reach them, will inevitably diverge. How can one truly support the other in fasting, confession, frequent Communion, or the rigorous spiritual life if they do not share the conviction of their efficacy and necessity?

3.  Raising Children: This is perhaps the most acute challenge in religiously mixed marriages. Parents have the sacred duty to nurture their children's souls in the Orthodox faith, to bring them to baptism, chrismation, and the Holy Eucharist, and to educate them in the traditions and teachings of the Church. When parents adhere to different faiths, children can experience confusion, internal conflict, and a weakening of their own spiritual identity. Often, one parent's faith is implicitly or explicitly undermined by the other, or compromises are made that dilute the children's spiritual formation. St. John Chrysostom himself, in speaking on family life, emphasized the crucial role of parents in transmitting the faith to their children, a task made immensely easier and more powerful when both parents are in agreement and actively participating.

4.  Sacramental Life: Our life as Orthodox Christians is deeply sacramental. Holy Communion is the "medicine of immortality." Confession is the pathway to healing and reconciliation. Chrismation seals us with the gift of the Holy Spirit. These are not mere rituals; they are the very lifeblood of our spiritual existence. A spouse who cannot partake in these mysteries with their partner creates a fundamental separation in the most intimate aspects of their spiritual lives.

✍🏾Implications for "Dating":

While dating might seem a less serious commitment than marriage, in the Orthodox Christian understanding, any serious dating relationship should be entered into with the potential for marriage in mind. Therefore, the same principles that apply to marriage apply strongly to dating. To pursue a relationship with someone of a different faith, knowing the Church's teaching and the inherent difficulties, is to set oneself on a path that is likely to lead to spiritual compromises or significant challenges.

✍🏾What if a relationship already exists?

If an Orthodox Christian finds themselves in a serious relationship with a non-Orthodox individual, the Church, with compassion, urges a path of prayer, discernment, and often, conversion of the non-Orthodox partner.

👉🏾Conversion: The hope is always that, through witnessing the beauty and truth of Orthodoxy, the non-Orthodox partner might, by God's grace and their own free will, choose to embrace the Orthodox Faith. This must be a genuine conversion of the heart, not merely a superficial agreement for the sake of marriage, as true faith cannot be coerced.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Four Main Purposes Found in the Consecration of the Liturgy

During the celebration of the Holy Liturgy, four essential spiritual elements are revealed:

1. Teaching (Education)

The Divine Liturgy contains the dogma and doctrine of the Church. The mysteries of the Holy Trinity, the Incarnation, the Body and Blood of Christ, and the honor of the Holy Virgin Mary are all proclaimed through the prayers of the Liturgy.

For example, when Abba Hiryakos composed the Liturgy of St. Mary, he clearly expressed the mystery of the Trinity and the divine role of the Theotokos.

2. History

Through the celebration of the fourteen liturgy, the faithful learn the history of the Church, the lives of the saints, the apostles, and the work of God throughout salvation history.

3. Spiritual Advice

The Liturgy teaches believers to love one another, to be patient, to live in unity, to fast, to pray, and to walk in holiness. These teachings are not given briefly, but deeply and repeatedly throughout the Liturgy.

4. Exhortation and Correction

The Liturgy also exhorts the faithful to examine themselves. For example, it teaches that if someone has a quarrel with a brother or sister, reconciliation must come before Communion. It reminds us of our relationship with others and our 
submission to God the Creator.

These four elements show that the holy Liturgy is a complete spiritual school for humanity.

✍🏾The Offering in the Liturgy

The Divine Liturgy is a communal prayer where readings, hymns, and sacrifices are offered by the priest, the deacon, and the faithful together.

The Church teaches:
“Do not stand naked before the prophet of God.”

✍🏾This means that no one should come before God without an offering. Even if a person has little, they should offer what they are able without shame. Offerings may include incense, raisins, bread, or other gifts.

✍🏾During the Liturgy, the priest prays specifically over the offerings of the faithful. If no one brings an offering, we must ask: for whom is this prayer said? Therefore, preparation for the Liturgy includes preparing an offering, according to one’s ability.

✍🏾Preparation for the holy Liturgy

When we come to church to participate in the Holy Liturgy, we must prepare ourselves in the following ways:

👉🏾To stand reverently and participate fully

👉🏾To listen attentively to the readings and apply them to our lives

👉🏾To receive Holy Communion for eternal life The Church teaches through hymnody that anyone who does not remain until the end of the Liturgy, who does not listen to the Holy Scriptures, and who does not receive Holy Communion without reason, separates themselves from the communion of the Church. Therefore, preparation is essential.

✍🏾Sanctification of the Five Senses in the Liturgy

During the Divine Liturgy, all five human senses are consecrate :

1. Sight (Eyes)

The faithful observe the priest’s movements at the altar.

These movements are not random; each has deep spiritual and mystical meaning. By seeing them, the eyes are sanctified.

2. Hearing (Ears)

Through hymns, prayers, Scripture readings, and proclamations by the priest and deacon, the ears are sanctified.

3. Smell (Nose)

The fragrance of incense sanctifies the sense of smell and symbolizes the prayers of the faithful rising to God.

4. Taste (Tongue)

By receiving the Holy Communion, the Body and Blood of Christ, the sense of taste is sanctified.

5. Touch (Hands and Body)

Touch is sanctified through bowing, prostration, kissing the Gospel, and receiving the priest’s blessing.

✍🏾The Liturgy as Complete Communion with God

✍🏾When all five senses are united in worship, the believer experiences full communion with God. This is the Divine Liturgy.

✍🏾The education received in the Liturgy is different from ordinary teaching. It is revealed by the Holy Spirit through generations of scholars and saints. The Gospel, Epistles, Acts, Psalms, and hymns are read melodiously, especially from the Psalms of David (Misbak).

Through continual participation in the Liturgy, a person spiritually learns the entire Bible from the Old Testament to the New Testament and lives the life of the angels on earth.

✍🏾Responsibility Toward the Next Generation

The Divine Liturgy is the greatest mystery of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Therefore, it is our responsibility to teach our children:

👉🏾To participate in the Liturgy

👉🏾To bring offerings

👉🏾To prepare themselves spiritually

👉🏾To receive Holy Communion

If we fail to pass this sacred tradition to the next generation, we risk losing what has been entrusted to us by the Fathers of the Church.

May this heavenly mystery, in which we unite with the angels and glorify our Creator, bring peace and strength to our homes and preserve the Holy Church without wavering.
