Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The word Ketera is derived from the Geʿez verb መከተር (meketer), which means to gather water, to restrain it, or to block its flow.

✍🏾On the eve of the Feast of Baptism, the Ark of the Covenant (Tabot) is taken out of the church and brought to a place where water is found, such as a river, spring, or prepared pool. The faithful of the area gather at that place and erect a tent (dass) near the water for the Ark to remain overnight. When no natural shelter exists, a tent is deliberately set up for this sacred purpose.

👉🏾Because spring water is often weak or limited, a well or pit is dug to collect the water. The water is then restricted and prevented from flowing away, so that it may be prepared and preserved for the baptismal celebration on the following day.

👉🏾Regarding the meaning of the word Ketera, Wazemaw Sergew (1981, p. 8) explains that Ketera comes from the Geʿez verb ketera, which carries the meaning of gathering, restraining, or enclosing, and is closely related to the sense of kebebe (to surround or enclose).

✍🏾Similarly, Kidane Wold Kifle (1948, p. 555) interprets the root “ketere” as meaning to block, stop, restrain, or forbid. Since the primary activity of the faithful on Tir 10 each year is the gathering and restriction of water for baptism, this day is appropriately named Ketera.

✍🏾The water is collected and prepared to be used as the baptismal font for the faithful, since the Feast of Baptism (Timket) is celebrated on Tir 11.

✍🏾The place where the Ark of the Covenant (Tabot) is kept overnight in a tent or temporary shelter, and where natural or gathered water is cleansed, preserved, or collected, whether from springs, rivers, or artificially prepared pools, is called the Bahire Tmket,Ark shelter .

✍🏾Sea (Bahir)

The Sea (Bahir) refers to a place where water is gathered, such as a reservoir or collected body of water prepared for baptism. In this sense, it is a “land of water”, a sacred space set apart for worship, prayer, and the mystery of baptism. It represents a sanctified world of water(mekane may, aleme may), prepared for holy use.

👉🏾During the reign of Saint Lalibela, the righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot, who traveled widely throughout Ethiopia preaching salvation and evangelism, blessed and sanctified the baptismal fonts in places such as Aksum, Mekelle, and Melrtule Maryam, strengthening the tradition of Ketera and Timket.

✍🏾Later, during the reign of Emperor Yekuno Amlak (1260–1275 AD), the righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot (1203–1204 AD) formally affirmed and ordered the continuation of the celebration that had already been practiced by the faithful under their spiritual care.

✍🏾The Tabots (Arks of the Covenant) were placed under the protection and care of the community and were brought to the baptismal sites for the celebration. Over time, the observance of the Feast of Baptism expanded, growing from a local religious practice into a national spiritual celebration.

✍🏾Although the Feast of the Baptism of the Lord had been observed as a public celebration since the time of Emperor Gebre Meskel, it was firmly established and systematized in the 15th century by Emperor Zara Yaqob (1426–1460 AD).

✍🏾Emperor Zara Yaqob decreed that:

✍🏾The Tabot should descend to the baptismal site on the afternoon of Tir 10, the eve of the Feast.It should remain there overnight.It should not return by the same route, so that the land would be blessed by its passage.

👉🏾Following this decree, Emperor Naod (1486–1500 AD) further commanded that all Orthodox Tewahedo believers should accompany the Ark of the Covenant both during its descent to the baptismal site and its return to the church.

✍🏾The faithfuls carrying the Ark of the Law (Tabot) out of the church with loud voices, ululation, and joyful proclamation, the faithful escort it to the Jordan of Baptism, where they remain overnight in vigil, prayer, and praise.

✍🏾Because more than one Tabot descends to the Jordan, this fulfills the word of God spoken to the prophet Moses:

“The Ark shall be a sign that I am with you.” (Exodus 25)
Just as the priests of the Old Covenant crossed the Jordan River carrying the Ark of the Law, so too the priests of the New Covenant, carrying the unchanging Ark, unite the Old Testament with the New Testament. 

👉🏾Remembering Jesus Christ as the foundation of the New Testament, the priests of the Church also journey to the Jordan, following His path.

✍🏾According to the great scholar Haregewein Ageze, the learned clergy spend the night teaching and proclaiming the Word of God appropriate to the feast. Likewise, ketera commemorates Tir 10 as the day on which our Lord Jesus Christ went from Galilee to the Jordan River to be baptized by Saint John the Baptist.

✍🏾Liturgical Order of the Eve of Baptism

✍🏾On the eve of the feast, Vespers begin at four o’clock in the morning in all local churches. The service continues with prayers proper to the feast, and the Holy Liturgy is celebrated. The priests who carry the Tabot abstain from Food, observe spiritual discipline, and offer prayers fitting to the sacred occasion.

✍🏾The Procession of the Ark

On the Ketera day, after the tent has been prepared, the water gathered, and everything arranged properly, the time comes for the movement of the Ark of the Covenant from the Church .

✍🏾The Tabots are:

👉🏾Covered with gold and silver cloths

👉🏾Adorned with beautifully embroidered priestly vestments
Priests and deacons, shining in their sacred garments, carry crosses (Metsor Meskel )and censers, and as they depart from the church toward the Abhirt (sanctuary or baptismal site), church bells ring everywhere, announcing the holy procession.

✍🏾Participation of the Faithful

#Baptism of #Christ

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾Meaning of Baptism

Baptism is one of the nine great feasts of our Lord Jesus Christ, foretold by the prophets and revealed in the Holy Gospel. The word baptism comes from the verb meaning to "Tetemke". Its meaning is to be fully immersed in water, usually in flowing water such as a river, spring, or lake. The baptism performed by the priests of the Church is a holy sacrament, distinct from all other forms of symbolic baptisms.

✍🏾 Baptism in the Old and New Testaments

✍🏾 In the Old Testament, baptism was a baptism of repentance. In the New Testament, baptism is the baptism of rebirth and adoption as children of God, beginning from infancy. However, the baptism of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is unique and unlike any other. Though He is God by nature, He humbled Himself, not seeking honor from humanity, but honoring humanity.

✍🏾 To be an example and a spiritual Father to us, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was baptized in the Jordan River by John the Baptist. Through His baptism, He revealed His natural Sonship and His divinity, testified by God the Father and the Holy Spirit. On that day, He sanctified the waters, and afterward He withdrew and began His fast .

✍🏾 The Law and the order that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ fulfilled were not fulfilled as something foreign or strange, like a guest who arrives unexpectedly.  He fulfilled the prophecies that were spoken beforehand, the examples that were foreshadowed, the appointed times that were counted, and the hope of salvation that was given to Adam from the beginning. The Holy Scriptures testify to this fulfillment and example as follows:

👉🏾“Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.”(Matthew 3:13; Mark 1:9; Luke 3:21; John 1:32)

👉🏾But John objected and said, “Does the Lord receive baptism from His servant? Should the servant baptize the Lord? Does the servant go to the Lord, or does the Lord come to the servant?”

✍🏾 When our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, came from Nazareth to visit Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, Holy Elizabeth said, “Why is this granted to me, that the Mother of my Lord should come to me?” Likewise, John expressed humility before Christ. But our Lord said to him, “This is our joy and our gladness:
 
✍🏾that you are proclaimed in the ministry of baptism and your honor is spoken of, and that I am baptized by the hand of a servant and My humility is proclaimed. Allow it for a time, for it is fitting for us to fulfill the prophecies of the prophets.”

✍🏾He was baptized once, not twice; willingly, not by force; in His human nature, not in His divinity. For He who is pure God had no need of cleansing, yet He accepted baptism to fulfill righteousness, to reveal humility, and to establish the sacrament for the salvation of humanity.

It was foretold by the prophets that John would baptize, and that the Lord Himself would be baptized by John. 

Therefore, our Lord said, “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness,” meaning that the prophecies spoken beforehand must be fulfilled.

This was done for the joy of the believers, so that when they are baptized, the Holy Spirit may come upon them. It was also for the joy of the Father, who testifies to His Son; for the joy of the Son, who reveals His obedience and humility; 

and for the joy of the Holy Spirit, who is manifested to the world.
When the Son was baptized in the Jordan River, God the Father bore witness from heaven, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” At the same time, the Holy Spirit descended in the form of a dove and rested upon Him. Through this divine manifestation, the unity and revelation of the Holy Trinity were made known.

Then our Lord said to John, “We must complete the work of righteousness that has begun; allow it for a time.” And John consented and baptized Him willingly, according to the will of God.

👉🏾John the Baptist said, “The Father is in You through the Holy Spirit, and You are in the Father through the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit is in You and in the Father. I baptize others in Your name, but in whose name shall I baptize You?”

👉🏾Our Lord answered him, saying, “The Son is blessed, and you are a priest to the world, according to the order of Melchizedek.”

✍🏾After this, they went down together into the water. As the Gospel says, “When our Lord Jesus Christ was baptized, He came up from the water” (Matthew 3:16), and “the heavens were opened to Him.” This opening of the heavens does not mean that heaven was physically closed and then opened. Rather, just as when a sealed vessel is opened its contents become visible, so also at the baptism of our Lord a hidden mystery was revealed. That mystery is the manifestation of the unity of the Holy Trinity.

👉🏾From this arises the question: Why did the Lord go from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized? Does a servant go to his master, or does the Lord go to His servant? Does the servant receive baptism from his master, or does the Lord receive baptism from His servant?

Our Lord’s coming was not for His own glory, nor merely for humility. 

👉🏾Rather, it was to set an example. If our Lord had said to John, “Come and baptize Me,” then kings, nobles, and rulers would later say, “Come to our houses and baptize us.” Instead, our Lord Himself went to John and was baptized, teaching us by example to go to the Church, where the priests are, and to receive baptism according to the order established by God.

✍🏾 The baptism of our Lord was not to add glory to Him, for He is already full of glory. Rather, it was to make the Jordan River a radiant womb, so that we, the believers, might be reborn of water and the Holy Spirit and enter the Kingdom of Heave

Question : why don`t we recite other prayers in holy lituargy

👉🏾Answer : My child, the Divine Liturgy is not an ordinary time of prayer. It is the highest and most perfect prayer of the Church, handed down to us by the Apostles and sealed by the Holy Spirit. When we stand in the Holy Liturgy, we are not standing alone as individuals, but together with the Church on earth and the Church in heaven.

For this reason, we do not recite personal or separate prayers during the Holy Liturgy. To do so would be to divide the heart and the attention. 

The Liturgy itself is a complete prayer: thanksgiving, repentance, supplication, praise, and sacrifice. In it, the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ are offered and received. There is no prayer higher than this on earth.
The fathers teach us that mixing other prayers into the Liturgy is like lighting a candle under the full sun. When the sun is shining, the candle adds nothing. The Holy Liturgy is that sun. If we participate in it with fear of God, faith, and love, our souls receive life itself.

This does not mean that personal prayer is unimportant. On the contrary, prayer is as necessary to our life as food and water. But every prayer has its proper time and order. Personal prayers belong before or after the Liturgy, at home, in the night, or in times of need. During the Liturgy, our prayer must be one with the prayer of the Church.

If there is a serious and compelling reason that prevents a person from offering private prayer on a certain day, this does not mean that God abandons them because they did not pray. God is merciful and knows our weakness. Nevertheless, we must never become careless, for prayer is the breath of the soul and without it the soul grows weak.

Therefore, my child, when you stand in the Holy Liturgy, stand fully present. Listen, respond, bow, repent, and receive grace. Do not add to it, and do not take from it. What the Church gives you there is more than enough for life and salvation.

✍🏾Question :  What is the role of our mother Mary in our salvation?

✍🏾Answer : My beloved child, may God’s grace and the boundless mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ ever dwell within your heart. Your question regarding the role of our Most Holy Mother Mary in our salvation is of profound spiritual importance, touching upon one of the most cherished doctrines of our Orthodox Faith. It is a question that requires deep reverence and careful elucidation.

As we journey together in understanding the mysteries of our faith, let us turn our gaze to the Mother of God, the Theotokos, for her role is central and indispensable in God's divine plan for humanity's salvation, though always understood in relation to her Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

1. The Theotokos: The Ark of the New Covenant and the Gate of Incarnation

Firstly and most fundamentally, the Most Holy Theotokos is the Mother of God (Theotokos in Greek, which means "God-bearer" or "she who gave birth to God"). This is her most exalted title, affirmed by the Third Ecumenical Council in Ephesus (431 A.D.). She is not merely the mother of Christ's human nature, but the mother of the Person who is both fully God and fully Man.

Her role in our salvation begins with her "Fiat" (Let it be done), her humble and free acceptance of God's will at the Annunciation: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word." (Luke 1:38, Septuagint) Without her "yes," without her pure and obedient vessel, the Incarnation of God the Word would not have occurred in the manner God ordained. She became the living Ark of the New Covenant, carrying within her womb the very Creator of the Universe, who took flesh from her pure blood.

2. The New Eve: Undoing Disobedience

The Holy Fathers often refer to the Theotokos as the New Eve. Just as the first Eve, through disobedience, brought sin and death into the world, leading to our condemnation, so too did the New Eve, through her perfect obedience and purity, become instrumental in bringing forth the New Adam, Christ, who would conquer sin and death. Her purity of heart and mind, her absolute devotion to God, made her worthy to become the vessel for salvation. We believe that she was chosen and preserved by divine grace, and that through the indwelling of the Holy Spirit at the Annunciation, she was made perfectly pure and sinless, a fitting dwelling place for God.

3. Her Participation in the Economy of Salvation

Our Mother Mary did not merely give birth to Christ and then disappear. She actively participated in the economy of salvation:

👉🏾At the Nativity: She brought God into the world.

👉🏾At the Presentation in the Temple: She offered Him to God and heard the prophecy of Simeon concerning the sword that would pierce her soul (Luke 2:35), foreshadowing her suffering at the foot of the Cross.

👉🏾At the Wedding at Cana: She interceded on behalf of others, prompting Christ's first public miracle: "Whatever He says to you, do it." (John 2:5) This is a profound lesson for us on obedience to Christ.

👉🏾At the Foot of the Cross: She stood steadfast, enduring unimaginable pain, truly sharing in the suffering of her Son for our salvation (John 19:25-27). This co-suffering, not co-redemption, further highlights her intimate participation.

4. Our Intercessor and Mother

Having completed her earthly course, our Mother Mary was assumed into heaven, body and soul (her Dormition). From her exalted position, she continues her maternal care for all humanity, especially those who call upon her Son. She is a most powerful intercessor before the throne of God. We seek her prayers, not because she grants salvation, but because her prayers, as the Mother of God, are especially potent and efficacious. She is our advocate, our solace, and a fount of mercy, always pointing us towards Christ, her Son and our God.

✍🏾Let us be clear, my child: Salvation comes only through our Lord Jesus Christ. He alone is the Redeemer, the Savior, the High Priest, and the Sacrifice. The Theotokos made the Incarnation of our Savior possible. She is the bridge between God and humanity, the scala coeli (ladder to heaven), through whom God descended to us and through whom we ascend to Him.

As our beloved St. John Chrysostom teaches us to honor the saints and especially the Theotokos: "Let us marvel at her, let us be astonished, let us adore her as the Mother of God; yet let us also imitate her virtuous life." She is the epitome of humility, purity, obedience, and self-sacrifice – a perfect model for every Christian soul striving for theosis.

Therefore, her role in our salvation is indispensable and glorious. She is "more honorable than the Cherubim and incomparably more glorious than the Seraphim," because she bore God Himself. Through her, Christ came into the world to redeem it.

May the prayers of our Holy Mother Mary ever uphold you.

For this reason, the church is filled with light through candles, oil lamps, olive oil, and even modern lamps. These lights are used during regular prayers, the Divine Liturgy, the reading of the Holy Gospel, before holy icons, and on the pulpit.

Light holds profound spiritual meaning because it is a divine command. From the very beginning, God revealed Himself through light:

“And God said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light. And God saw that the light was good” (Genesis 1:3–4).

✍🏾The early Christians also prayed with light, as Scripture tells us:“There were many lamps in the upper room where they were gathered” (Acts 20:8).

✍🏾Above all, the church must be filled with light because it is the dwelling place of God, who is holy and luminous. Our Lord Jesus Christ said, “I am the light of the world” (John 8:12), and the Apostle John teaches, “God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all” (1 John 1:5). In the Book of Revelation, the Church itself is called a lampstand. Saint John saw Christ standing among the seven golden lampstands, which represent the seven churches (Revelation 1:20).

✍🏾The mystery of lamps lit with olive oil is especially deep. In the Old Testament, oil was used to anoint priests and kings, symbolizing the presence and power of the Holy Spirit. Scripture says, “Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon David from that day forward” (1 Samuel 16:13). For this reason, oil and light in the church remind us of our anointing by the Holy Spirit and His work within us.

✍🏾The candle and lamp burning in the church symbolize the mercy of the Holy Spirit working in our hearts and our continual remembrance of God. Their constant flame reminds us that God’s protection never leaves us. The light of the church also represents the righteous and the martyrs. Our Lord said, “You are the light of the world. Let your light so shine before men” (Matthew 5:14–16), and Scripture speaks of the righteous shining like stars (Daniel 12:3). They are described as lamps placed on a lampstand (Matthew 5:15).

✍🏾Therefore, lighting lamps before the icons of the saints and martyrs signifies that they were lights in their deeds and words. They burned with the fire of God’s love and became light to the world through their faith and sacrifice. This light reminds us of their suffering and their glory, as the Lord said, “The righteous will shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father” (Matthew 13:43), and John the Baptist was called “a burning and shining lamp” (John 5:35).

✍🏾Our Lord also commands spiritual vigilance, saying, “Let your waist be girded and your lamps burning” (Luke 12:35). Thus, when we see the lamps burning in the church, we are reminded to remain spiritually awake and prepared for the coming of Christ.

✍🏾When a candle is lit during the reading of the Holy Gospel, it symbolizes the guiding power of God’s Word in our spiritual journey:

👉🏾“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path” (Psalm 119:105).

👉🏾“The commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes” (Psalm 19:8).

✍🏾Therefore, the lights in the Holy Liturgy are not mere customs or decorations, but sacred symbols filled with divine meaning. They proclaim the presence of God, who is Light without darkness, and reveal the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church. The burning lamps remind us of Christ, the Light of the world, of His life-giving Word, and of the saints and martyrs who shone through faith and obedience.

✍🏾By filling the church with light, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church teaches her children to walk in spiritual vigilance, purity, and righteousness.

During the season of Asteryo , the Church celebrates the great revelation of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, through which the mystery of the Holy Trinity was made known. However, although the Virgin Mary is inseparably united with the mystery of Christ’s incarnation, the Church does celebrate her feast during this season as “Asteryo Mary.” Each feast in the Church is honored according to its own spiritual meaning and appointed time.

✍🏾 The Departure and Glory of the Holy Virgin Mary

Our Mother of God, the Holy Virgin Mary, lived on this earth in holiness and obedience, bearing suffering and pain for the sake of humanity’s salvation. After completing her earthly life, she rested in glory according to the guidance of the Holy Spirit. Though she died in the flesh, she was honored by God, and like her Son, she was raised in glory. According to the tradition of the Church, this took place in the holy month of Nehase.

✍🏾 The Life of the Holy Virgin Mary

The Holy Virgin Mary lived:

👉🏾3 years with her parents,

👉🏾12 years in the Temple,

👉🏾33 years and 3 months with her beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ,

👉🏾15 years under the care of the holy Evangelist Saint John after the Ascension of our Lord.
Thus, she lived a total of 64 years in this world in purity and holiness.

✍🏾Her Repose

The Holy Virgin Mary passed away on Tir 21/ 49 A.D after completing her life in holiness and obedience to God.

✍🏾 Why the Church Celebrates This Feast

All Christians are called to celebrate this holy feast, because our Holy Orthodox Tewahedo Church, guided by the Holy Spirit, has established an orderly and spiritual tradition for us. The Ascension (Repose) of the Holy Virgin Mary is a feast celebrated by the faithful, and in Ethiopia, as well as throughout the entire Orthodox Tewahedo world, it is observed with great reverence, joy, and devotion.

✍🏾 The Meaning of the Celebration

We do not celebrate this feast merely to remember the passing of our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary. Rather, we celebrate it with hope in her intercession, trusting in her prayers and motherly care. As we remember her holy repose, we ask that our Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary, may remember her country Ethiopia, and through her prayers may God grant peace, love, unity, and stability to her people.

May she also intercede for us before her Son, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of our sins and the salvation of our souls.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

👉🏾Saint Ura'el is known as a helper in times of trouble, a guide in darkness, and a protector of God’s faithful people.

The #Seven #Times of #Prayer: #Sanctifying the Whole Day.

Question:Can someone explain what we should pray about during the seven prayers each day?

Answer:My child, the Seven Times of Prayer were not given to burden the body, but to heal the soul and gather the scattered hours of our day back to God. The Church, like a wise and patient mother, divided time itself and placed prayer inside it, so that no hour would remain empty of remembrance.

Each prayer hour is not random. Each one is rooted in creation, salvation, suffering, love, repentance, hope, and rest. When we pray them, we walk through the life of Christ and the history of humanity in one single day.

1.Yengeh (11:00–12:00) – Why We Pray at This Hour

We remember our Savior Jesus Christ, who loved us to the point of death, standing silently before Pilate without judgment. At this hour, we ask the God who grants rest to also grant rest to our souls.
This is the time when our father Adam was created, reminding us of our own beginning and God’s original purpose for humanity.

Morning Prayers 

Especially if we did not pray during the night, it is good to pray in the morning. These may include:

👉🏾The Psalms of David

👉🏾Wudase Maryam

👉🏾Arganon

👉🏾Bartos Prayer

👉🏾Seife Selassie

👉🏾Seife Melekot

Since morning is a time of renewal and alertness, and the hours are open to us, we should pray according to our strength and love for prayer.

2.The Third Hour Prayer (3:00 AM) – Why We Pray

At this hour:

👉🏾Our mother Eve was created.

👉🏾The Prophet Daniel prayed and was saved from the mouth of the serpent.

👉🏾Our Lord Jesus Christ was flogged without sin before Pilate.

👉🏾The Holy Apostles received the Holy Spirit on Mount Zion, and the 72 languages were revealed.

👉🏾The Virgin Mary received the Good News from the Archangel Gabriel.

Because of this, we pray especially to the Virgin Mary and the Archangel Gabriel at this hour, asking her Son to intercede for us.
These prayers should not exceed 30 minutes. If time or strength is limited, it is sufficient to pray:

👉🏾Selam Eleki three times

👉🏾One Abune Zebesemayat

3.The Sixth Hour Prayer (6:00 AM)

This is the hour when we remember:

👉🏾Christ was stripped to clothe us with the robe of glory.

👉🏾He was crowned for our sake.

👉🏾He accepted bitter suffering and death.

👉🏾The Virgin Mary endured deep sorrow.

At this time, it is good to pray:

👉🏾Sene gologota

👉🏾seyfe melekot

As the Psalmist says:
“Evening and morning and at noon I will pray, and He shall hear my voice.” (Psalm 54:17)

This hour is also dangerous spiritually, as demons are active, so we must strengthen ourselves through prayer.

4.The Ninth Hour Prayer

This is the hour when our Lord revealed His love for humanity by dying on the Cross.It is also the hour when the holy angels carry human prayers to the Creator.

Because it is the hour of Christ’s death, we pray with repentance, remembering our own death, asking forgiveness for our sins, and glorifying God.

5.The Eleventh Hour Prayer

This hour reflects rest after labor. Just as people receive their daily bread, the faithful await their eternal reward at the Second Coming of Christ.For this reason, the prayer of this hour reminds us of the Second Coming.

At this time, it is appropriate to pray:

👉🏾 wudase Maryam

👉🏾mihla tselot (ምህላ)

6.The Evening Prayer

This is the hour when God established the order of prayer through the saints and among the people.

It is a prayer to the God of peace, asking Him to grant us peace of soul and body.

Recommended prayers include:

👉🏾wudase maryam

👉🏾Anqetse birhan

👉🏾ywedswa

If one was unable to pray in the morning, this hour is especially suitable. It is also good to pray the Arganon used by our forefathers.

7.The Night Prayer (6:00 PM)

This is the hour when we remember the expected coming of our Lord.

It is also the hour when sleep and distraction are strongest, making prayer more difficult and more valuable.

At this time, we may pray as we are able:

👉🏾wudase maryam

👉🏾Bartos Prayer

👉🏾Arganon

👉🏾Sene Golgotha 

👉🏾Prayers to the Seven Archangels

What Should We Pray During the Seven Times?

The Church does not imprison us with one fixed prayer per hour. She gives us life, not chains.
At each of the seven times, we may pray:

👉🏾Wudase Maryam and Tselote Maryam

👉🏾Abune Zebesemayat (አቡነ ዘበሰማያት)

👉🏾The Psalms of David (መዝሙረ ዳዊት, Mezmure Dawit), divided through the day

👉🏾Gospel prayers, short supplications, praises, and Gedlat

✍🏾These are the prayers by which saints repented, wept, endured, and were sanctified. When we pray them, we do not stand alone. We stand inside the same river of prayer that carried the righteous before us.

✍🏾The Heart of the Teaching

God does not count our prayers. He receives our hearts.The value of prayer is not in length, but in attention.Not in quantity, but in humility.Not in perfection, but in repentance and faith.Even a short prayer, offered with a watchful heart, is precious before God.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾According to the canon of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, there are seven major fasts observed by the faithful.

✍🏾The Fast of Nineveh is one of the seven fasts whose start date is calculated using the Mebaja Hamer—the combined result of the Tewosak and the yearly Metqi.

✍🏾Nineveh was a great and ancient city, founded by Nimrod, a mighty ruler, on the banks of the Tigris River, as recorded in Genesis 10:11–12.

Nineveh was known for its beauty, size, and strength.

The length of its city wall was approximately 12 kilometers, making it one of the largest cities of the ancient world.

👉🏾It served as the capital city of Assyria, just as Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia or other modern capitals serve their nations.

✍🏾Assyria traces its origin to Asshur, one of the sons of Shem, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:22).

👉🏾Asshur became the forefather of the Assyrian people, whose land was located in Upper Mesopotamia.

✍🏾Nineveh became the political and military center of the Assyrian Empire.

Nineveh served as the capital of the powerful Assyrian Empire. During its peak, it frequently challenged and attacked the Kingdom of Israel. 

✍🏾 This occurred after the reign of Solomon's son, Rehoboam, when the nation split into two weakened states: the Northern Kingdom (Israel) and the Southern Kingdom (Judah).

✍🏾 ​In 720 B.C., the Assyrian Empire—with Nineveh as its heart—conquered Samaria, the capital of the ten Northern tribes. They deported the population and scattered them across five unfamiliar foreign lands, where they eventually integrated and became known as the "Lost Tribes." In their place, the Assyrians resettled people from other regions in Samaria.

✍🏾 ​The Assyrian Empire also oppressed the Southern Kingdom of Judah, at one point even taking King Manasseh captive to Babylon. However, they were unable to destroy the capital city, Jerusalem. During the reign of King Hezekiah, the Assyrians insolently challenged God. As recorded in the Holy Scriptures:

✍🏾​"That night the angel of the Lord went out and put to death a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up the next morning—there were all the dead bodies! So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there." (2 Kings 19:35-36)

​Until its fall to the Babylonian Empire in 612 B.C., Nineveh was renowned as "The Great City." It officially became the capital of Assyria around 700 B.C. during the reign of King Sennacherib.

About “#Adam’s #Fall and #Christ’s #Victory:

✍🏾Question :-Question for those that Believe you have To be from certain Christina denomination to be saved. 

Through one man Adam, all humanity fell, everyone, everywhere, regardless of location, nationality, religion, belief, or morality. Death, suffering, and corruption spread through the devil’s use of one man.

Through one man, Jesus Christ, salvation was accomplished for all humanity, because He assumed human nature, healed it, and restored it.So here is the real question 

If the fall destroyed all humanity through Adam, does Christ’s redemptive power fall short of that destruction if only a few receive it through baptism, knowledge of the Gospel, or being part of a Christian denomination?

What about those who never heard it? 

If Christ healed human nature itself, shouldn’t that healing truly reach all, everywhere, without limitation?

If the devil could affect everyone through one man, can Christ’s victory be considered complete if  we teach it only saves some ?

✍🏾Answer :- My Child, At the beginning of your question, you said that this question is directed to those who believe that a person must belong to a specific Christian denomination in order to be saved. Therefore, we will answer you according to the teaching of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

✍🏾From your question, it is clear that you are a thoughtful reader. This is a good and deep question, not asked lightly. It comes from reflection and concern for the justice and completeness of God’s salvation.

✍🏾It is true that through Adam and Eve, death entered the entire human race. This affected all people, without distinction of religion, race, place, or morality. Because of Adam’s sin, Paradise was closed, and all humanity was destined to descend to Sheol. However, we must understand this correctly. The righteous did not suffer the torment of hell, nor were they separated from God’s care. As the Scripture says, “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them” (Wisdom 3:1). Yet, Paradise remained closed until Christ.

👉🏾 Just as Adam’s sin affected everyone, so Christ’s salvation also reached everyone.

✍🏾Answer 1

We Orthodox believe that through the incarnation, suffering, death, and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, the entire human race was saved from the sin of Adam and Eve and from the death that came through them. This salvation from Adam’s sin is universal. Every human being, regardless of religion, is freed from the condemnation of Adam through Christ. We are not judged for Adam’s sin, because Christ has already healed human nature.

👉🏾 The Church teaches that baptism, repentance, faith, learning the Gospel, and good works are necessary not to remove Adam’s sin, but for salvation from personal sins and from hell. This must be clearly understood. Christ has already saved all humanity from Adam’s sin. As the Scripture says, “He who believes and is baptized will be saved, but he who does not believe will be condemned.”

Answer 2

We do not believe that there is anyone today who has not, in some way, encountered the Gospel. Even before modern technology, the apostles preached throughout the world. Today, the Gospel is accessible everywhere. As our Lord said in the Gospel of Matthew, the Gospel would be preached to all nations, and the Gentiles would hear it. Hearing alone is not the way of Salivation . Acceptance remains a matter of the heart.

Answer 3

Yes, the Gospel has gone out into the world, and through Christ the whole world has been saved from Adam’s sin.

👉🏾Answer 4

We do not teach that only a few are saved. We teach that Christ, by becoming man, saved the entire human race from the sin of Adam and Eve. However, after this universal healing, God gave us a law to guide our lives. While Christ cleansed us from Adam’s sin, He also calls us to obedience. Salvation is not automatic for the sins we personally commit. Whoever fulfills the law through faith and works will be saved, and whoever rejects it will be condemned.

As the Apostle James says, “As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead” (James 2:26). The Scriptures also teach us to pray, to fast, and to live a life of repentance. Our Lord Himself said, “Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life” (John 6:54). Eternal life means living in communion with God and being saved from hell.

This is the teaching of the Church, my child. It does not limit Christ’s victory, nor does it deny God’s mercy. It shows us the path by which healed humanity lives in the salvation Christ has already accomplished.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Fast of Nineveh was a fast of repentance observed by the people of the city of Nineveh. By the time of the holy Prophet Jonah, the wickedness and evil deeds of Nineveh had risen up to heaven before God.

✍🏾 Because of this, God sent the Prophet Jonah to Nineveh to warn its people, calling them to repentance so that they might be saved from the coming wrath.

✍🏾 Nineveh was located about 800 kilometers from Gath-Hepher, the place where the Prophet Jonah was born and raised. Although Jonah first withdrew from his mission, he later obeyed the command of God. As the Scripture says:

👉🏾“Jonah began to enter the city a day’s journey, and he cried out and said, ‘Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.’”(Jonah 3:4)
According to this verse, the Prophet Jonah went through the city of Nineveh, proclaiming the word of God.

✍🏾 The response of the people is written clearly in the Holy Scripture:“So the people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.”(Jonah 3:5)

👉🏾Through repentance, fasting, humility, and turning back to God, the people of Nineveh were reconciled with Him and were saved from destruction and divine wrath.For this reason, the Church remembers this repentance and calls it the Fast of Nineveh.

👉🏾 What Was the Sin of the People of Nineveh?

The sin of the people of Nineveh is not listed one by one in the prophecy of Jonah. Instead, it is described in a general but very serious way. God says:

“Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness has come up before Me.”(Jonah 1:2)

✍🏾 The Scripture does not specify their sins in detail in the Book of Jonah. However, the words “their wickedness has come up before Me” clearly reveal the greatness and severity of their sin. A sin that reaches heaven is not small, hidden, or accidental.

✍🏾 Although their sins are not listed in Jonah, they are described more clearly in other prophetic books.

👉🏾 The Witness of the Prophet Nahum

✍🏾 The Prophet Nahum speaks openly about the sins of Nineveh. He begins his prophecy by saying:

“The burden against Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.”(Nahum 1:1)

One of the major sins of Nineveh described by Nahum is conspiring against God.

👉🏾“There is one who plots evil against the Lord, a wicked counselor.”(Nahum 1:11)

✍🏾Conspiring Against God

The kings of Nineveh during the time of Prophet Jonah humbled themselves, repented, and saved their city from destruction through fasting and prayer. But the rulers who lived before and after that generation became known for cruelty, arrogance, and rebellion against God.

✍🏾They trusted in idols, glorified violence, and opposed the will of the Most High. In their pride, they behaved as though God could be challenged, ignored, or replaced.
This is what it means to plot against God. Not only with words, but with actions, systems, and attitudes that deny His authority.

✍🏾A Warning for All Generations

This lesson is not written for Nineveh alone.
Those who oppose God through injustice, pride, corruption, cruelty, or rebellion should take warning. Whether in leadership or among the people, no one escapes accountability before God.

✍🏾 Do not miss the opportunity to repent and be reconciled with God. The leaders of Nineveh became an example by humbling themselves first and leading their people in repentance. Through this, they saved both their city and their nation from the wrath of God.

✍🏾 No matter how great the sin, do not allow it to push you away from repentance. God does not hate the sinner, but the sin. What destroys us is not falling, but refusing to return.

✍🏾God’s Open Call to Repentance

The Lord Himself calls us, saying:

“Come now, and let us reason together,” says the Lord.“Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow;though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land;
but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword.”
(Isaiah 1:18–20)Nineveh teaches us an uncomfortable truth humans dislike.

✍🏾The leaders of conquered cities were tortured, mutilated, and publicly humiliated before being killed. Although the people of Nineveh repented at the preaching of the prophet Jonah, they did not persevere in repentance. Their wickedness once covered them completely. ✍🏾 The man of God, the prophet Nahum, speaks plainly about Nineveh, saying:

Such pride and bloodshed rose as a cry before God. ✍🏾Saint Cyril, Bishop of Jerusalem, taught about the life of Our Lady in the Temple in his sermons.

He explains that Joachim and Anna had the custom of visiting their daughter once each month. They would bring her what she needed, and the holy Virgin would serve in the Temple together with the older virgins, who taught her the work of the hands and the ways of service.When she reached the proper age, she would go to the Temple by herself.

✍🏾 No man would see her except the priests and her father. The Virgin Mary lived within the Temple, and the Archangel Gabriel would approach her with a sweet fragrance. Her beauty was beyond measure, and the Temple was filled with angels because of the fragrance of her purity. Saint Cyril describes her life in detail, saying that people would come only to hear her holy words.

✍🏾The Teaching of Saint Demetrius of Antioch
(256 AD)

👉🏾Saint Demetrius, Archbishop of Antioch, also taught concerning the life of Our Lady in the Temple.

✍🏾When her mother Anna placed her at the door of the Temple before the priests, the child entered and went as far as the veil of the altar, where sacrifices were offered to the Lord. After entering, she did not turn back to go outside, nor did her mind dwell on her family or on earthly matters.

✍🏾As she grew and reached the age of eight or ten, she became an example to all the priests. They feared to gaze upon her, for her body was pure and her heart firmly established in the Lord.
She was pure in body and soul. She never turned her face toward the outside of the Temple, never saw a stranger, and never looked upon the face of a man. She lived in holiness, serving God continually in the Temple. Her garment reached her forehead, and her veil covered her eyes.

✍🏾She did not use eye makeup, nor did she adorn her face with ornaments or flowers. She did not wear sandals on her feet, nor bracelets or jewelry on her arms and hands. She did not seek rich food, did not walk in the marketplaces of the city, and had no interest in worldly affairs.

✍🏾She never exposed herself to defilement, nor examined her body with vanity, bearing witness to her perfect purity and holiness during her life in the Temple.

✍🏾The Teaching of Saint Cyril of Alexandria(376–444 AD )

Saint Cyril of Alexandria taught the women gathered in the Temple about the humble life of the Holy Virgin, saying:

👉🏾“All women who desire virginity should follow the example of Mary, the Mother of our Lord.”
He called attention to her simple way of eating and her habit of sleeping on the ground. She had no desire for the pleasures of this world, and her name was continually on the lips of the priests because of her holiness.
She never washed her body in public baths. She never adorned herself with makeup, eyeliner, ointments, or brightly colored clothing, as was common among women of her time.

👉🏾She never tasted wine and lived in constant expectation of her Creator, who created all worlds. She would sit facing the east in prayer. She did not meet or speak with anyone except her mother and father, and she became a teacher and example to the pure virgins.

✍🏾The prophet David says:

👉🏾 “The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree; he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon. Those who are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God.”(Psalm 91:12–13)

This prophecy was fulfilled in the life of Our Holy Lady, the Mother of God, who lived in the Temple in purity and holiness for twelve years, becoming the dwelling place prepared for the Incarnation of the Word.

✍🏾The Doctrine of Mary in Orthodox Faith

The dwelling place of the prophets, the root of the apostles, and the mystery of the Church of the saints is the doctrine of the Holy Virgin Mary. It is impossible to correctly teach the doctrine of Christ without rightly teaching the doctrine of Mary.

✍🏾Throughout the history of Christianity, the first error of many heretics was their rejection or misunderstanding of the doctrine of the Holy Virgin Mary. Because of this, they also failed to believe rightly in Christ. If they had held a sound faith concerning Mary, they would not have fallen into heresy concerning Christ.

👉🏾The doctrine of Mary and the doctrine of Christ cannot be separated. They are united.Whatever is said about the Holy Virgin, whether rightly or wrongly, directly affects the faith concerning Christ Himself.

✍🏾The Error of Nestorius

Nestorius failed in his faith concerning Christ because he struggled to accept the Holy Virgin Mary as Theotokos , Mother of the Word, and Mother of God. His error concerning Mary led him into error concerning Christ. This shows clearly that the doctrine of Mary is inseparable from the doctrine of Christ.

✍🏾Mary and the Work of Salvation

When we speak of God’s work of salvation, we cannot leave the Holy Virgin Mary aside. She is the one who bore Him in her womb, endured suffering and persecution, and followed Him in humility. She stood by the cross on the day of His crucifixion and never departed from Him.

✍🏾The work of salvation

 accomplished on the cross began in the womb of the Holy Virgin. The Lord took flesh from her, blood from her, and a human soul from her. He offered this flesh and blood on the cross for our salvation and then gave it back to us as the Bread of Life.

✍🏾Her Unique Holiness

From the moment this great mystery was fulfilled in her, the Holy Virgin Mary became the dwelling place of the divine mystery. For this reason, she is praised above all creation. In our hymns and liturgy, the Church praises her immediately after the Holy Trinity.

✍🏾Saint David prophesied concerning her, saying:

👉🏾“His foundations are in the holy mountains.The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God.”(Psalm 87:1–3)

✍🏾She carried the divine fire in her womb, as she herself proclaimed:

“My soul magnifies the Lord,and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,for He has regarded the lowliness of His handmaiden.
For behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed,for He who is mighty has done great things for me,and holy is His name.”(Luke 1:46–49)

✍🏾The Great Works Done in the Holy Virgin

The great works God accomplished in the Holy Virgin Mary include:

✍🏾She was preserved from the darkness of the former corruption.

✍🏾She was kept free from the dominion of the devil.

✍🏾She was freed from the curse of the law.

✍🏾She carried in her womb Him whom the cherubim bear, the seraphim serve, the angels fear, and whom heaven and earth cannot contain.

Therefore, like Saint David, we praise her, saying:“Wonderful are the things done for you, O Virgin Mary.”


Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, is pure, holy, holy, holy, meaning she is set apart, distinguished, honored, chosen, and exalted above all women. This is because the curse that fell upon fallen humanity did not dominate her soul. Although she took true human flesh like all of us, her soul was preserved by the grace of God.

To reveal this mystery, the wise Solomon spoke prophetically, praising her complete beauty and purity, saying that her beauty is perfect in every aspect. This does not refer merely to physical beauty, but to the harmony of her body, soul, and heart, all preserved in holiness.

The Holy Church teaches and believes that the Virgin Mary was a virgin before conception, during conception, and after childbirth, according to the prophetic words of Scripture (Isaiah 7:14; Ezekiel 44:1–4).

This confirms that she was found to possess a pure body, a pure soul, and a pure heart, united as one.

Therefore, when the wise man says, “You are without blemish,” we understand this in harmony with the words of the Archangel Gabriel, who said to her:
“Rejoice, you who are full of grace, the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.”

This greeting was spoken because the angel Gabriel was sent to a virgin. This virginity refers not only to the body, but also to the soul. Her soul was untouched by defilement, filled with grace, and preserved in holiness by God.

For this reason, the wise man rightly declares:
“My beloved, all is beautiful in you.”

Yet, through perseverance:

👉🏾They reject empty human praise.

👉🏾They labor faithfully in all circumstances.

They are finally welcomed into eternal joy with the holy angels.Though they may be insulted by people during their service, they will be honored openly by God at His coming.

✍🏾The Unfaithful Servant

The third servant was foolish, for he buried the talent that had been given to him and did no work with it.

👉🏾Instead of using the grace of service according to his ability, he hid his talent. He was unable to endure the arguments and slander of the hypocrites, the temptations of the world, and the desires of the flesh. When his master questioned him, he did not acknowledge his weakness but responded with false accusations against his master.

✍🏾Such servants are like this: they blame others for their failures but do not examine themselves or correct their faults. Therefore, the Lord said to His angels:

👉🏾“Take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents. For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.”(Matthew 25:28–29)

There are some who criticize this saying without understanding its meaning. This teaching does not refer to material wealth, but to spiritual grace and service.From this, we also understand that the end of an unprofitable servant, whether priest, teacher, or believer, is judgment if they fail to fulfill their calling. As it is written:

👉🏾“Cast the unprofitable servant into outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”(Matthew 25:30)

If the servant who did not use the talent given to him was judged by the Lord, what will be the fate of those who not only neglect their own calling, but also hinder the service of others? Those who, out of ignorance and envy, bury the grace given to true servants and oppose the work of righteousness what will they say when they stand before the Lord?

Therefore, let us understand that we must not become instruments of such people, who rush to suppress and destroy the work of righteousness.

The unfaithful servant in the parable was separated from the faithful servants and was not found worthy of the Kingdom of Heaven. His condemnation came because he failed to use the talent entrusted to him.

✍🏾The Responsibility of Priests

Priests have a greater responsibility than other believers. The Church Fathers teach that if they fulfill their duties faithfully, according to the grace given to them, their reward and glory in the Kingdom of Heaven will be greater.

As Saint Paul teaches:

👉🏾“There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.”(1 Corinthians 15:41)

If priests do not fulfill their duties, if they fail to strengthen those who have fallen away from the faith, and if they do not guide those who are weak in conduct, then they cannot enter the Kingdom of Heaven. For just as their honor is greater than that of other believers, so also is their responsibility.

✍🏾Faith and Works Together

The parable of the unfaithful servant teaches us that no one is saved by position alone. A priest, teacher, or servant cannot enter heaven without fulfilling their calling.

According to Holy Scripture, salvation requires both faith and righteous conduct. Conduct without true faith, or actions done outside the true faith, do not lead to salvation.

Salvation is given by the grace of God and is not earned by human effort. Yet, as Saint James teaches:

“Faith without works is dead.” (James 2:26)

Therefore, it is impossible for a person to be saved by faith alone without righteous conduct.
The Example of the Five Virgins
The five virgins had lamps, which represent faith, but they lacked oil, which represents righteous conduct. Because of this, they were shut out of the Kingdom of Heaven.

👉🏾In the same way, teachers and priests must first unite faith with conduct before taking on their ministry. It is not possible to truly serve as a priest or teacher without being a faithful believer.
True servants are those who live in genuine faith first, and then teach and serve others from that foundation.

✍🏾The corrupt servants of our time are those who say, “Do for others what you do not do for yourself.”

✍🏾In every age, there are those who treat service not as an act of faith, but as a duty for personal gain. They see it as a source of income, recognition, or obligation, rather than a calling rooted in true belief.

Such people:

👉🏾Teach others to repent, yet do not repent themselves.

👉🏾Teach others to pray and prostrate, yet lack true prayer in their hearts.

👉🏾Teach others to fast, yet do not fast sincerely.

👉🏾Teach others to give alms and tithes, yet do so only for public praise.

Even when they perform good works, they do them to be seen by others, not for the glory of God. They instruct the faithful to avoid vanity, yet they themselves seek honor and recognition.

✍🏾True priests and servants are first true believers before they teach or serve. They are free from pretense and deceit, and their service is sincere and without reproach.

✍🏾Servants receive their reward from their Master, but the grace and the fruit of their service do not belong to them.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the website of John the Repentance ,we greet you with the greetings of God.Today, according to the above topic, we present this important lesson and invite you all to read it carefully and learn from it.

Our Lord rose from the dead as the firstfruits of our resurrection. Through His resurrection, we are assured that we too shall rise and not remain in death forever.

✍🏾 The resurrection of our Lord is not like the resurrection of Lazarus. Lazarus was raised on the fourth day, but he later died again, and his resurrection required someone else to raise him.

In contrast, our Lord rose by His own divine power. His resurrection is eternal and not followed by death. He did not need anyone to raise Him. Therefore, He is rightly called the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

👉🏾 “For we know that Christ, being raised from the dead, will die no more. Death no longer has dominion over Him.” (Romans 6:9)

✍🏾 Christianity cannot be understood apart from the resurrection. After confirming and believing in the resurrection, the Apostles boldly went out to preach to all nations.

👉🏾 “If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen… and your faith is futile… But now Christ is risen from the dead and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.” (1 Corinthians 15:13–20)

✍🏾 For this reason, the Holy Church includes the resurrection of the dead among the essential pillars of faith.

2. The Resurrection Made Us Live in Hope

A person without hope lives a miserable life and is focused only on earthly things. But we Christians, through the hope given to us by the resurrection of Jesus Christ, endure all the challenges of this earthly life while looking forward to eternal life with Him.

✍🏾 Just as a deer longs for streams of water, so we strive to live in righteousness, always setting the Kingdom of Heaven before our eyes.

✍🏾 Even when our loved ones depart from this life, we do not grieve like those who have no hope.

 👉🏾“But we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who have fallen asleep, that you may not grieve as others who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep in Jesus.”(1 Thessalonians 4:13–14)

3. The Resurrection Granted Us Freedom

Because of the sin of Adam and his descendants:

👉🏾 The gate of Paradise was closed to him

👉🏾 He fell under the harsh dominion of the devil

👉🏾 Death reigned over him, and he lived without freedom for 5,500 years

✍🏾 But through the resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ:

👉🏾 The gate of Paradise was opened

👉🏾 The dominion of the devil was overthrown and his power weakened

👉🏾 Death was defeated and its authority abolished

✍🏾 Having received freedom, humanity now proclaims:

👉🏾 “O death, where is your sting? O Hades, where is your victory?”(1 Corinthians 15:55)

✍🏾 The Holy Fathers teach that just as the dragon worshipped by the Babylonians was destroyed when it consumed the food prepared by the Prophet Daniel, in a similar way death was defeated when it “swallowed” the body of the Lord. Instead of holding Him, death was overcome, and the Lord rose victorious.

✍🏾 Therefore, Saint Paul warns us not to abandon this freedom and return again to the slavery of sin:

👉🏾 “For freedom Christ has set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not be entangled again with a yoke of slavery.”(Galatians 5:1)

The Apostle Paul clearly teaches:

“If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen. And if Christ is not risen, then our preaching is empty and your faith is also empty… But now Christ is risen from the dead, and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.”(1 Corinthians 15:12–20)

Therefore, the Ascension of our Lord established the Church as a spiritual kingdom on earth, through which believers are prepared and led toward the kingdom of heaven.

2. The Resurrection Gives Us Dignity and Boldness

Through the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, our shame has been removed, and we are given the courage to walk with our heads held high. What was once a source of fear and weakness has been transformed into confidence and hope.

The world has seen many who claim authority and many religious movements, yet none can be compared to the true Christ as revealed in His Word. Likewise, no Church stands as the pure and holy Orthodox Tewahedo Church, which is founded upon the sacrifice of Christ and confirmed by His Resurrection.

The founders of earthly movements remain in their graves; their bodies have returned to dust. But when we look to Golgotha in Jerusalem, we do not find our Lord in the tomb. His grave is empty.

“He is not here; for He is risen, as He said.” (Matthew 28:6)

This truth is eternal and unchanging. It is a message to be proclaimed in every generation.

In our present time, when many are weighed down by fear and uncertainty, the voice of the Church continues to declare: Christ is risen from the dead.

The Resurrection is the confirmation of the truth of our faith and the seal of our salvation.

3. The Resurrection Strengthens the Weak

The greatest strength of the weak is faith in a mighty God. Our God is powerful and great , and through His Resurrection, our Lord Jesus Christ became the source of confidence and strength for all who are weak.

Before the Resurrection, the Apostle Peter was overcome by fear and denied Christ even before a servant girl (Matthew 26:69). But after the Resurrection, and through the fullness of the Holy Spirit, he stood boldly and proclaimed the Savior and the divinity of Jesus Christ before thousands (Acts 2:14–42).

This transformation shows that the Resurrection of Christ truly gives strength to the weak, turning fear into courage and doubt into bold faith.

4. The Resurrection Gives Power to Stand for the Truth

The Resurrection of our Lord does not raise us only to knowledge, but to true faith. Many people love the truth only when it costs them nothing. But the power of the Resurrection strengthens believers to remain faithful, even when the truth demands sacrifice.

If our Lord Jesus Christ had not risen from the dead, His disciples would not have gone out to preach, nor would they have stood boldly before others. But because He rose, they proclaimed Him without fear.

The Apostle Peter, who once denied Christ out of fear, later stood firm in the truth and gave his life for it. He would not have offered himself for something false.

Likewise, the other disciples endured persecution and even death, because they were certain of the Resurrection.

Therefore, the Resurrection of Christ gives believers the courage to stand for the truth, no matter the cost.

5. The Resurrection Proclaims Our Own Resurrection

Before the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, all human beings lived in fear of death—fear of the grave, of hell, and of the separation of the soul from the body. But our Lord Jesus Christ, having conquered death through His Resurrection, lifted humanity above the power of the grave and hell.

His Resurrection not only freed the soul but also gave hope to the body, which will not remain forever in the grave.

✍🏾Physical death is not destruction. It is a transition—a change of dwelling, a rest, and a sleep until the time of resurrection.

Our Lord Jesus Christ did not rise to demonstrate His power, but to declare our own resurrection:

“But now Christ is risen from the dead, and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.” (1 Corinthians 15:20)

He rose by His own authority, and we also will rise by His authority. We will not remain in corruption or decay.

Jesus Christ is the firstborn from the dead, and we too will follow Him. Our perishable bodies will be raised incorruptible, and what was subject to death will be raised into eternal life.

 “For we know that if our earthly house… is destroyed, we have a building from God, eternal in the heavens.” (2 Corinthians 5:1–5)

✍🏾 The Victory of Christ Over Death

Our Lord Jesus Christ, through His Resurrection, conquered not a temporary enemy but an eternal one—death—which cannot be overcome by human wisdom or power.

The great kings who ruled mighty empires were able to conquer nations, yet none of them could conquer death. They ruled for a time, but eventually they all submitted to it. However, our Lord Jesus Christ rose from the dead and conquered death itself.

The #Church Built in the Name of the #Holy #Virgin# Mary


Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the website of John's Repentance, we greet you with the peace and blessings of God.

Today, under the above topic, we present the sacred mystery that our Lord revealed to His holy apostles, and through them to us, concerning the Most Holy Virgin Mary and the Church built not by human hands, but by the hands of God Himself.

This is not an ordinary story, but a holy event recorded in the Synaxarion, faithfully preserved by the Church, and illuminated by divine grace. May all who read it receive spiritual understanding and be strengthened in faith.


On Sene 20, in the district of Chalcedon in Caesarea Philippi, our Lord Jesus Christ Himself built a church not of wood, nor of clay, nor of water but by three  stones, drawn together by divine command. This church was built in honor of His Holy Mother, the Virgin Mary, the All-Immaculate Theotokos. It stands among the holiest of her feast days, a monument not only of stone, but of heaven's descent upon earth.

In the eighth year of the Lord’s reign, the apostles Paul and Barnabas, having preached the Gospel and baptized many Gentiles in Philippi, desired to build a holy place where the new believers might worship. But they did not act without heavenly guidance. Saint Peter, the Chief of the Apostles, and Saint John the Beloved, were summoned. And then O awe-striking wonder! the Lord, gathering both the living and the dead, brought together all His apostles in a divine convocation.

Christ our God appeared and said, “I have gathered you to teach you the manner in which churches are to be built throughout the earth in the name of My Mother.” He took them eastward and, with divine majesty, moved three stones into one foundation. He measured it: 24 cubits in height and 12 in width, a mystery in number and in spirit. These stones, soft as wax under divine fire, were fashioned into a church by the hands of the apostles, according to the command and guidance of the Lord.

On the following day, Sene 21, the Lord descended again with His Holy Mother, the Virgin Mary. She stood as the new Ark of the Covenant, holier than that of Moses. He ordained the apostles: Saint Peter as priest, Saint Stephen as deacon, and sanctified the Eucharistic mystery, causing the heavenly bread and cup to descend into that first church. And thus, the apostolic priesthood and the mystery of the Eucharist were sealed under the name of the Theotokos.

What then do these sacred elements mean? Why such precise numbers and symbols? The Church built 24 cubits high mirrors the 24 heavenly prophets, who in the time of kings foretold the coming of Christ. The 12 cubits in width mirror the 12 holy apostles, who bore the Gospel to all lands. The three stones are a figure of the All-Holy Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit one essence, undivided, eternal.

But more still is hidden in this holy teaching:

The church, being divided into three parts, reflects the ark across three divine ages:

1. The Ark of Adam—the beginning of humanity, fallen yet destined for glory.

2. The Ark of Moses—the Law, a shadow of the greater things to come.

3. The Ark of Christ—the fulfillment, in whom all is completed.

And even the angelic orders are shown as a divine reflection of the priestly ranks of the Church:

Angels = Singers

Princes = Anagogians

Elders = Deacons

Powers (haylat )= Priests

Arbab = Commissaries

Cherubim, Seraphim = Bishops

These ranks are not merely symbols, but living realities. Just as the celestial orders do not usurp one another, so also in the Church no lower order may ascend presumptuously to the higher, and no higher may neglect the service to the lower. Yet all serve in harmony, according to grace and rank, in unity and obedience.

And what shall we say of the heavenly vision seen in the Seraph of the Aramaic?
It is the image of the Church itself:

The Throne of Light – the altar of Christ

The Ark of Light – the Theotokos

The Veil of Light – the mystery of the Incarnation

The Four Pillars – the four evangelists and chief bishops

The Twenty-Four Elders – the company of apostolic bishops around the throne of God (cf. Revelation 4:4)

Let the weak in faith be awakened!  For this is no tale of old, but a present reality: the Church is born of heaven, and the Virgin is her crown. She is not honored for her own sake alone, but because in her the fullness of Christ was pleased to dwell, and in her name, He established the visible sign of salvation on earth the One, Holy, and Apostolic Church.

Let us therefore honor the feasts of Sene 20 and 21 with awe and devotion, not as a relic of the past, but as a living remembrance that Christ built His Church in the name of His Mother, and through her intercession, continues to build it even now in every land and heart.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

What Does #God #Desire from Us?

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the website of John the Repentance ,we greet you with the greetings of God.Today, according to the above topic, we present this important lesson and invite you all to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾 "Fasting is the mother of prayer, the sister of repentance, the source of tears, and the ancient foundation of every good work." (Koquiha Religion, )p. 318.*

This teaching reminds us that the spiritual life begins with humility, repentance, and a sincere desire to draw near to God.

✍🏾 What Does God Desire from Us?

Above all, God desires:

👉🏾 Our heart

👉🏾 Our will

👉🏾 Our faith

God does not seek outward appearances or empty words. He desires a heart that loves Him, a will that longs to obey Him, and faith that trusts in His promises.

✍🏾 What Is Meant by "Our Will"?

The will that God seeks is not merely human strength or determination. Rather, it is our sincere desire to draw near to Him. Even if we are weak, God strengthens those who genuinely seek Him. He grants both the desire and the strength to accomplish His holy will.

As the Apostle Paul writes:

> "For it is God who works in you both to will and to work for His good pleasure."(Philippians 2:13)

God never forces anyone to be reconciled with Him. Instead, He patiently waits for us to turn to Him willingly. He desires our free response of love and repentance.

✍🏾 Our Responsibility

Although God gives us strength, He also calls us to cooperate with His grace. Our willingness to work with Him demonstrates the sincerity of our repentance and our desire to live according to His commandments.

Therefore, once we have resolved to follow God, we must begin every good work with prayer, asking Him to strengthen us and help us overcome every obstacle that stands in our way.

✍🏾 The Counsel of the Holy Fathers

Saint Basil the Great teaches:

 "Keep your heart at peace. Be diligent to become the least of all and the servant of all. Be slow to engage in idle talk, but be wise through the knowledge of the Holy Scriptures, for they lead to salvation."

Likewise, the Holy Apostle James instructs us:

"Therefore, my beloved brethren, let every person be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger." (James 1:19)

God seeks neither riches nor worldly achievements from us. He desires a humble heart, a willing spirit, and steadfast faith. When we offer these to Him with sincerity, He Himself works within us, strengthens us through His grace, and leads us on the path of salvation.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.
